### DEF-112 — Bulk Product ID import capped at 100 rows due to per-row HTTP requests hitting AspNetCoreRateLimit

- **Date:** 2026-05-06
- **Severity:** High (blocks the use case CR-016 was scoped around — bulk-import of partner-onboarding ASIN lists)
- **Status:** Fixed (pending UAT — requires dev-server restart to load the C# changes)
- **Reporter:** Shawn — `localhost:5101/Certificate/Edit/26-0106` import of 1000-row test CSV. First 100 rows imported, next 900 returned `"Unknown error"`.

**Symptom:** Importing >100 product IDs into a certificate failed every row past the 100th. UI reported `Imported 100 product ID(s). 900 failed: Row 101 ... Unknown error; Row 102 ...`. Exact 100/900 split was the giveaway — that's a per-minute rate-limit cap being hit.

**Root cause:** Two compounding bugs.

1. **Frontend was firing one HTTP request per row.** `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js#applyImport()` looped over every selected row and did a separate `fetch('/api/productids', POST)` for each. For 1000 rows that's 1000 separate API calls.
2. **AspNetCoreRateLimit caps `*/api/*` at 100 req/min per IP** (configured in `appsettings.json:96-99`). Request 101 onward returned 429. The fetch wrapper read `await response.text()` for the body but the actual error string came back empty for 429s, so the user-facing toast said `"Unknown error"` instead of `"429 Too Many Requests"`.

**Fix:** Three coordinated changes.

1. **New JSON-body bulk endpoint.** `Controllers/Api/ProductIdApiController.cs` adds `POST /api/productids/certificate/{certificateId}/bulk` accepting `BulkProductIdImportRequest` (`{ items: ProductIdImportItem[], overwriteExisting: bool }`). Replaces 1000 individual POSTs with one request — dodges the rate limit by design.
2. **Frontend rewritten to use bulk.** `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js#applyImport()` now splits selected rows into `creates` and `updates`. Creates go in one bulk POST; modifications still PUT individually (small count, no rate-limit risk). The replace-all toggle now passes `overwriteExisting: true` to the bulk endpoint instead of looping individual DELETEs from the browser.
3. **Service-layer pre-fetch optimization.** `Services/ProductIdService.cs#ImportProductIdsAsync` no longer calls `CreateProductIdAsync` per row (which itself fired 3 DB queries + a SaveChanges). Now: pre-fetches existing rows, parent cert status, and max display order in 3 queries total; does duplicate detection against an in-memory dictionary; queues all entities; commits a single batched SaveChanges. Improvement for 1000-row import: ~4000 DB roundtrips → ~3 + 1 batched insert. Should complete in 1-2 seconds instead of timing out.

**Header tolerance (bonus, related to DEF-111):** The file-based `/api/productids/certificate/{id}/import` endpoint now accepts both legacy template headers (`Value`, `ProductName`, `ProductSku`) and new-template headers (`Product ID`, `Product Name`, `SKU`). Backend `DownloadSampleCsv` aligned to the new column order.

**Files touched:**
- `Controllers/Api/ProductIdApiController.cs` — added bulk endpoint and `BulkProductIdImportRequest` DTO; updated DownloadSampleCsv header.
- `Services/ProductIdService.cs` — rewrote `ImportProductIdsAsync` to pre-fetch + batch insert; made `ImportFromCsvAsync` header lookup tolerant.
- `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js` — rewrote `applyImport()` to use the bulk endpoint.

**Test plan:**
1. Stop the dev server (it's holding `bin/Debug/net8.0/GCCWebApp.exe` — current PID 37876). Run `dotnet build` then `dotnet run --urls "http://localhost:5101"`.
2. Navigate to `/Certificate/Edit/26-0106`. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+F5) so the browser picks up the new JS.
3. Click **Import** in the Product ID Manager toolbar; pick `C:\Users\swest\Downloads\product-ids-sample-1000-asins.csv`.
4. Preview should show `1000 New, 0 Modified, 0 Errors`.
5. Click **Apply Import**. Expect: success toast `Imported 1000 product ID(s)` (no failures, no rate-limit error). Table reloads showing 1000 rows.
6. Inspect browser DevTools Network tab — only **one** request to `/api/productids/certificate/26-0106/bulk`, not 1000 to `/api/productids`.
7. Inspect server log — should show `Bulk import for certificate {id}: 1000 succeeded, 0 failed`.
8. Edge case: re-import the same file. Default mode (Add) should preview all 1000 as duplicates and report 1000 errors `already exists on this certificate`. Replace mode should silently keep them (no errors).

**Found by:** Shawn during DEF-111 retest with the 1000-ASIN test file generated 2026-05-06.

### DEF-113 — Same per-row HTTP-POST anti-pattern across 4 admin imports (Companies, Tags, Products, Users)

- **Date:** 2026-05-06
- **Severity:** High (blocks bulk-onboarding workflows on every admin import surface in the app, identical root cause to DEF-112)
- **Status:** Fixed (pending UAT — requires dev-server restart to load the C# changes)
- **Reporter:** Shawn — proactive sweep after DEF-112 fix

**Symptom:** After fixing DEF-112 on the Product ID import, an inventory of the rest of the app surfaced four more import flows using the same broken pattern: one HTTP POST per row in a `for await` loop. Affected surfaces:

| Surface | URL | Old endpoint per row | Frontend |
|---|---|---|---|
| Companies | `/Company/Management` | `POST /Company/SaveCompany` | `companyManagement.js#applySelectedImport` |
| Tags | `/Admin/Tags` | `POST /Admin/CreateTag` | `tags.js#applySelectedImport` |
| Products | `/Admin/ProductManagement` | `POST /Admin/CreateProduct` | `productManagement.js#applySelectedImport` |
| Users | `/Admin/UserManagement` | `POST /Admin/CreateUser` | `userManagement.js#importCSV` |

In dev, all four were exposed to the localhost IP rate cap of 200/min (`appsettings.json:112-124`), so any import >200 rows would fail rows past 201 with empty `"Unknown error"` strings (same as DEF-112's diagnostic). Per-row pattern was also slow (~10s per 100 rows) regardless of rate-limit hits.

**Root cause:** The frontend pattern of `for (const row of rows) { await fetch('/...', {body: row}) }`. Identical to DEF-112.

**Fix (universal pattern):** For each surface, three coordinated changes:
1. JSON-body bulk endpoint that accepts pre-parsed rows + replace flag (where applicable).
2. Service-layer optimization: pre-fetch existing rows + reference data once, in-memory dup detection, batched `SaveChangesAsync`. Dropped from N×4 DB roundtrips to ~3 + 1 batched insert.
3. Frontend `applyImport()` rewrite: collapse N requests into 1 bulk POST for creates; per-row PUT for the small "modified" set.

**Per-surface specifics:**
- **Companies** — new `POST /Company/BulkImport`, dup key `Name` (case-insensitive). Replace-all supported via `overwriteExisting` flag. Single bulk audit entry. Files: `Services/ICompanyService.cs`, `Services/CompanyService.cs`, `Controllers/CompanyController.cs`, `wwwroot/js/admin/companyManagement.js`.
- **Tags** — new `POST /Admin/BulkImportTags`, dup key `Name + TagType` (case-insensitive — Internal/External tags are independent namespaces). Tightens contract: existing `CreateTagAsync` had no dup check. TagType normalized to lowercase to match prod data. Files: `Services/IAdminService.cs`, `Services/AdminService.cs`, `Controllers/AdminController.cs`, `wwwroot/js/tags.js`.
- **Products** — new `POST /Admin/BulkImportProducts`, dup key `Name + CompanyId`. Pre-fetches Companies + ProductTypes as dictionaries for FK resolution. Replace-all NOT supported (mass-deactivation risk on typo). Bonus fix: the previous JS payload dropped `companyName` and `productTypeName` entirely — products imported as orphans. New JS sends them. Files: `Services/IAdminService.cs`, `Services/AdminService.cs`, `Controllers/AdminController.cs`, `wwwroot/js/admin/productManagement.js`.
- **Users** — new `POST /Admin/BulkImportUsers`, dup key `Email` (case-insensitive). Pre-fetches Users + Companies + Roles. BCrypt password hashing kept inline (CPU-bound, ~50ms/row). Replace-all NOT supported (locked-out-admin risk). New `BulkImportUserItem` DTO uses string-based references (`CompanyNames: List<string>`) which the service resolves to FK IDs in memory. Bonus fix: `userManagement.js#importCSV` was parsing a 9-column legacy format that no longer matched the 7-column template — every column was silently mis-mapped. Aligned to template format. Files: `Services/IAdminService.cs`, `Services/AdminService.cs`, `Models/AdminModels.cs`, `Controllers/AdminController.cs`, `wwwroot/js/admin/userManagement.js`.

**Tracking decision:** all 4 surfaces logged under one DEF-113 since they share root cause + fix pattern.

**Test plan:**
1. Stop the dev server; `dotnet build` then `dotnet run --urls "http://localhost:5101"`.
2. For each test file in `C:\Users\swest\Downloads\`:
   - `test-companies-250.csv` → `/Company/Management` → Import. Expect 250 created, 0 errors. One request to `/Company/BulkImport` in DevTools Network tab.
   - `test-tags-250.csv` → `/Admin/Tags` → Import. Expect 250 created, 0 errors. One request to `/Admin/BulkImportTags`.
   - `test-products-250.csv` → `/Admin/ProductManagement` → Import. Pre-req: `Amazon` company and `Personal Care` product type must exist; otherwise rows fail validation cleanly with name-resolution errors.
   - `test-users-250.csv` → `/Admin/UserManagement` → Import. BCrypt hashing 250 passwords takes ~12s server-side. One request to `/Admin/BulkImportUsers`.
3. Re-run any of the above. Expect all 250 to fail with "already exists" — confirms within-batch and cross-batch dup detection works.

**Found by:** Shawn — "let identify them and we need to test all of them" — proactive request after DEF-112 fix.

### DEF-162 — Main nav bar misaligned with page content (flush left edge instead of inside `.page-container`)

- **Date:** 2026-05-07
- **Severity:** Medium (cosmetic, but global — affects every authenticated page across all roles)
- **Status:** Fixed
- **Reporter:** Shawn — Cert single view screenshot, `https://gccwebapp.com/Certificate/CertificateSingleView/26-0157`

**Symptom:** The main navigation bar (`Certificates`, `Products`, etc.) renders flush against the left viewport edge instead of aligning with the `<h1 class="page-title">` and the rest of `.page-container` content. Visible on every page that uses `_Layout.cshtml`.

**Root cause:** `Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:155` was missing the closing `>` on the `<div class="nav-wrapper …">` opening tag:

```cshtml
<div class="nav-wrapper @(User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated != true ? "nav-anon" : "")"
    <nav class="main-nav" aria-label="Main navigation">
```

Browser parsers treat `<nav`, `class="main-nav"`, `aria-label="Main navigation"` as junk attributes on the div until they hit the first `>`, then drop the `<nav>` entirely. The `.nav-links <ul>` ends up directly inside `.nav-wrapper`, which has no `max-width` or horizontal padding — so links extend to viewport edge while `.page-container` (max-width 1800px, padding 0 40px) and `.main-nav` (same) sit further inset.

**Fix:** Closed the `nav-wrapper` div tag. One-character change. With the `<nav class="main-nav">` element actually rendering, its `max-width: 1800px; padding: 0 40px` matches `.page-container` exactly, so the nav links now align with `.page-title` on every page.

**File:** `Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:155`.

**Test plan:**
1. Hard-refresh `/Certificate/CertificateSingleView/26-0157` while signed in as `external` (or any authenticated role).
2. Confirm `Certificates` link aligns horizontally with the `Certificate Details` h1.
3. Spot-check a page in each role: `/Certificate/CertificateTileViewExternal` (External), `/Certificate/CertificateTileViewInternal` (Analyst/Admin), `/Admin/UserManagement` (Admin).
4. View source — confirm `<nav class="main-nav">` opens correctly and is a child of `.nav-wrapper`.

**Found by:** Shawn — single view screenshot.

The remaining columns are accepted (no validation error) but not yet written.

### DEF-164 — Anonymous certificate file endpoints serve PDFs of non-public certs (Draft / Hold / Suspended / Revoked / Expired)

- **Date:** 2026-05-08
- **Severity:** Critical (information disclosure — internal lifecycle PDFs harvestable by unauthenticated callers)
- **Status:** Fixed
- **Reporter:** Internal security audit (`audit/role-management-audit-2026-05-08.md` finding F-C-002 / F-C-003)

**Symptom:** Three `[AllowAnonymous]` endpoints on `CertificateController` served any certificate's uploaded PDF without checking whether the certificate was in a publicly visible status:

- `GET /Certificate/Download/{number}` (line 1506) — by certificate number
- `GET /Certificate/ViewCertificateFile/{id}` (line 1573) — by integer ID, inline display
- `GET /Certificate/DownloadByNumber/{number}` (line 1655) — by certificate number, delegates to `Download`

Certificate numbers are sequential (`YY-NNNN`) and integer IDs are trivially enumerable. An anonymous attacker iterating those identifiers could pull every Draft, Hold, Suspended, Revoked, or Expired certificate PDF — none of which the business considers publicly viewable.

**Why this slipped through:** The companion entry point `CertificateSingleView` (line 200) DOES correctly enforce `CertificateStatusHelper.IsPubliclyVisible(...) && !isExpired` for unauthenticated callers, but the three file-serving endpoints below it never received the same guard. Same vulnerability class as DEF-103 (Partner API status leak) — a contract enforced on the "list" surface but missed on a parallel "single resource" surface.

**Root cause:** Direct file-serve endpoints were originally written before the `PublicStatuses` concept formalised, and were never revisited when `IsPubliclyVisible` was added to `CertificateStatusHelper`. `[AllowAnonymous]` was kept (correctly) so verifiers without accounts can still download *publicly visible* certs from the Verify URL — but the status filter that makes that decision was missing.

**Fix:** Mirror the `CertificateSingleView` guard at all three endpoints. For unauthenticated callers only, check `IsPubliclyVisible(certificate.Status) && certificate.ExpirationDate >= BusinessToday`. Authenticated callers (Admin / Analyst / External / Partner) keep their existing access — they retain the legitimate need to view non-public certs through their respective workflows. `DownloadByNumber` gets its own explicit guard even though it delegates to `Download`, so the protection cannot be quietly lost in a future refactor (DEF-103 history).

**Files:** `Controllers/CertificateController.cs` (3 edits — lines 1506, 1573, 1655 region).

**Test plan:**

1. **Anonymous, public cert:** `GET /Certificate/Download/24-0001` (or any cert in `Active` / `Client Approved - Paid` etc. with a future expiration) — still downloads.
2. **Anonymous, Draft cert:** find a Draft cert number in dev (e.g. via `SELECT TOP 5 Number FROM Certificates WHERE Status = 'Draft'`) → request `GET /Certificate/Download/{that-number}` in incognito → expect `404 — Certificate {n} is not currently available for public download.`
3. **Anonymous, Expired cert:** find a cert with `ExpirationDate < TODAY` → expect 404 with same message.
4. **Authenticated Analyst, Draft cert:** sign in as `analyst / TestPass123!`, hit the same Draft cert URL → still serves the PDF (no regression for internal workflows).
5. **Anonymous, ViewCertificateFile by integer ID:** `GET /Certificate/ViewCertificateFile/{id-of-Draft-cert}` → expect 404 (NOT placeholder image — placeholder is only for missing-file case).
6. **Anonymous, DownloadByNumber:** same as #2 but via `/Certificate/DownloadByNumber/...` — expect 404 even though the inner `Download()` would also block.
7. Build: `dotnet build` → 0 C# errors (file-lock errors from a running `dotnet run` instance are not compile errors).

**Out of scope (separate audit findings):**

- F-C-001 (`TestController` missing auth), F-C-004 (`CertificatesApiController` accepts `?userRole=` from query string), F-H-001..F-H-005 — tracked as separate items in the audit report; will be addressed in follow-up DEFs.

**Found by:** Internal security audit run on 2026-05-08, before next UAT cycle.

### DEF-165 — Usability-contract batch: Product Management template, Cert table sort (Product Category + multi-value cols), Replace All toggle discoverability

- **Date:** 2026-05-08
- **Severity:** High (functional — controls don't do what their labels promise; erodes user trust)
- **Status:** Fixed
- **Reporter:** Shawn (verifying QC log items pre-UAT) + Carly (DEF-159 originally)

Four sub-items grouped because they're all the same defect class — the UI says X but the control does Y. Fixed in one batch.

**Sub-item A — Product Management import template doesn't match the Add New Product modal**

Verifying the QC item's "Fixed" claim showed it wasn't actually fixed. Three problems:

1. `Controllers/ProductController.cs:880` server endpoint emitted 7 columns including `Status` — but the Add New Product modal had `Status` removed back in QC #92.
2. `wwwroot/js/admin/productManagement.js:538` class method emitted a *different* 5-column CSV (`Name, Company, Description, Product Type, Status (Active, Inactive)`) — missing Category and Subcategory entirely.
3. Both fired on a single click — `Views/Product/Management.cshtml:35` had inline `onclick="downloadImportTemplate()"` (server endpoint) AND productManagement.js auto-bound the class method via `addEventListener`. Same duplicate-handler pattern that was fixed earlier this month for the Export button.

Fix: server endpoint now emits the 6-column header that mirrors the modal (`Name,Company,Description,Category,Product Type,Subcategory`). The JS class method is now a one-line `window.location.href = '/Product/DownloadProductImportTemplate'` — single source of truth, both pages get the same template, the duplicate handler becomes a no-op (browser dedupes the navigation).

Files: `Controllers/ProductController.cs:880`, `wwwroot/js/admin/productManagement.js:538`.

**Sub-item B — Internal cert tile: Product Category column sorts by Product Type**

`wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view-internal.js:636-637` had both `productCategory` and `productType` mapped to the backend key `'product-type'`. The backend never had a `'product-cat'` case at all, so even a corrected frontend would fall through to the default sort. Carly's report: "Carly Test and Electronics randomly show in middle of list" when sorting Product Category — exactly what you'd expect when the column is actually sorting by Product Type.

Fix: frontend `productCategory` now maps to `'product-cat'`, with a corresponding `'product-cat-za'` in the reverse-sort map. Backend `Controllers/Api/CertificateTileInternalApiController.cs` adds `'product-cat'` and `'product-cat-za'` cases sorting by `c.ProductCategory.Name` with a fallback to `c.Product.Category.Name` (matches the existing pattern used by `product-type` and `product-sub`).

Files: `wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view-internal.js:636,684`, `Controllers/Api/CertificateTileInternalApiController.cs:692-695`.

**Sub-item C — Internal cert tile: multi-value sort columns return arbitrary "first value"**

The backend cases for `int-tag`, `ext-tag`, `asin`, `upc`, `gtin`, `ean`, `cert-sub` all used the shape:
```csharp
c.Tags.Where(t => t.TagType == "internal").Select(t => t.Name).FirstOrDefault() ?? ""
```
No `OrderBy` inside the subquery. EF returned whatever the DB picked first — usually physical-row order. Two certs with the same internal-tag set inserted in different orders sorted differently. Same defect for ASIN/UPC/etc when a cert has multiple Product IDs of the same type.

Fix: every multi-value subquery now has an inner `.OrderBy(...)` before `.FirstOrDefault()`, so the per-cert "first" value is deterministic (alphabetic). Direction of the column sort is unchanged — only the inner-pick is now stable.

File: `Controllers/Api/CertificateTileInternalApiController.cs:700-721` (7 subqueries hardened: `ext-tag`, `int-tag`, `asin`, `upc`, `gtin`, `ean`, `cert-sub`, plus their `-za` reverse counterparts).

**Sub-item D (DEF-159 reframe) — Replace All Product IDs toggle was invisible to the user**

DEF-159 was opened by Carly as "build a Replace All UX" — but the feature already existed: `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js:1408+` reads `#overwrite-existing-toggle` and runs the replace-all path. The defect was discoverability: a small unstyled checkbox with the text "Replace all existing" sat in the modal footer next to the Download Template button. Carly imported a 1-row file in default (append) mode, hit a duplicate-key collision, and concluded "Replace all doesn't work."

Fix: in `Views/Shared/_ProductIdManager.cshtml:315-317` the toggle is now a pill-shaped chip with an amber border and `fa-exchange-alt` icon, label expanded to "Replace all existing IDs with this file", and the tooltip explains the two modes explicitly: "When checked: this import file is the new full list. Existing Product IDs not in the file will be deactivated. When unchecked (default): rows in the file are added or updated; nothing is deactivated." No JS or behavior change — the underlying replace-all logic is unchanged.

File: `Views/Shared/_ProductIdManager.cshtml:310-322`.

**Test plan:**

1. **Template (sub-item A)** — Sign in as `analyst`. `/Product/Management` → click Template. Open the CSV in a text editor: header should be exactly `Name,Company,Description,Category,Product Type,Subcategory` (single line, no trailing newline expected, no sample rows). `/Admin/ProductManagement` → click Template. Same file. Both pages now produce one identical download per click.
2. **Sort Product Category (sub-item B)** — `/Certificate/CertificateTileViewInternal` as analyst. Click Product Category column header. Rows should sort A→Z by Product *Category* (not Type). Click again → Z→A. Click Product Type column → resets, sorts by Type. Verifies the two columns are now distinct.
3. **Multi-value sort (sub-item C)** — Find a cert with two internal tags (e.g. via SQL: `SELECT TOP 1 CertificateId FROM CertificateTags WHERE TagType ...`). Click Internal Tag header — order should be deterministic across repeated page reloads. Same for ASIN if any cert has multiple ASINs.
4. **Replace All toggle visibility (sub-item D)** — Open `/Certificate/Edit/{any-cert}`, scroll to Product Identifiers, click Import, choose a CSV. In the preview modal, the Replace All toggle should now visibly stand out (amber/cream pill in modal footer). Hover the label — tooltip should explain both modes. Toggle off → import adds rows. Toggle on → import deactivates anything not in the file.

### DEF-181 — QC #108 self-test surfaced two defects in the User import template/parser

**Date:** 2026-05-11 | **Status:** FIXED 2026-05-11 | **Severity:** Medium | **QC Ref:** #108 (rigorous re-test) | **Note:** Originally numbered DEF-166 in error (collided with the cert-tile-perf entry above); renumbered 2026-05-11.

Shawn asked for rigorous testing of QC #108 after it was marked resolved. Authored a new Playwright NUnit suite (`GCCWebApp.UAT.Tests/Tests/Admin/QC108UserImportTemplateTests.cs`, 8 tests) and ran it against `localhost:5101`. First run: 6 passed, 2 failed — both real defects, both fixed in the same session.

**Sub-item A — Template CSV header was malformed (8 columns when parsed)**

The 7th header `Company Access (semicolon-separated names, or "All")` contains an unescaped comma. `headers.join(',')` produced a row that any RFC-4180-compliant parser (Excel included) splits into 8 columns, surfacing a phantom 8th header to the user.

Fix: `wwwroot/js/userManagement.js` — `downloadImportTemplate()` now wraps any header field containing a comma or quote in RFC-4180 quotes with internal quotes doubled. The header line still reads identically when un-escaped, but CSV parsers now see exactly 7 columns.

**Sub-item B — Template advertised "All" as a valid value, but parser rejected it**

The template hint says `Company Access (semicolon-separated names, or "All")`. The JS preview parser (`resolveCompanyIds`) already short-circuits `"All"` → every-company-IDs, but the server-side parser at `Controllers/AdminController.cs` `ImportUsers()` didn't. A row with `Company Access = All` hit the company-name-lookup path → no match → 0 companies assigned (or `Company 'All' not found` error). The template hint lied.

Fix: `Controllers/AdminController.cs` — `ImportUsers()` now special-cases `companyAccessRaw.Equals("All", OrdinalIgnoreCase)` → assigns every `Company.Id`. Matches the JS preview behavior. Same `Company Access` semantics now apply whether the user uses the UI import flow (JS preview → batch `/CreateUser` calls) or POSTs the file directly to `/Admin/ImportUsers`.

**Test plan:**

1. **Template malformation (sub-item A)** — `/Admin/UserManagement` → click Template. Open in Excel: should see exactly 7 columns (Name, Email, Role, Password, Status, RequirePasswordReset, Company Access). Pre-fix: 8 columns with a phantom `or "All")` last header.
2. **"All" semantics (sub-item B)** — Modify template: add 1 row with `Company Access = All`. Click Import → preview shows the row assigned to all companies → confirm → user is created with company-checkboxes for every company. POST the same file directly to `/Admin/ImportUsers` (e.g., curl with auth cookie + antiforgery): user is also assigned to every company. No `Company 'All' not found` error.
3. **Regression** — Repeat TC-QC-108 baseline test plan (headers-only template, no sample row, "Company Access" column on UI/export/template, 5/1 client reply satisfied).
4. **Automated:** `dotnet test --filter QC108` against TEST_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5101 → 8/8 passing.

**Found by:** Anuki internal QA — Shawn-directed rigorous re-test of QC #108 (2026-05-11). Did NOT come from client.

### DEF-235 — `Permissions-Policy` response header is duplicated on prod (DEF-107 fix regressed / re-injected)

> ⚠️ **DEF-NUMBER COLLISION (flagged 2026-06-02).** This number is also used by the sustained-load `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` entry earlier in this file (~line 115). Both were opened in the same 2026-06-02 governance sweep. **Proposed resolution:** renumber THIS (Permissions-Policy) entry to **DEF-237**, keep the connection-refused entry as DEF-235 (it's more cross-referenced — e2e-smoke-plan, batch-restart mitigation). Awaiting Shawn's ok before renumber (ripples to `predeploy-record-2026-06-june-batch.md` + the Gate-5 governance note). Tracked in the June predeploy record blocker #3.

> ✅ **UPDATE 2026-06-02 — fix is in the working tree and folded into the June deploy batch.** The `web.config` `<httpProtocol><customHeaders>` block (the second injection source) has already been removed (web.config lines 22-31 are now an explanatory comment); `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` is the single source. Localhost re-verified: `HEAD /` emits exactly 1 of each security header (`Permissions-Policy count=1`). `web.config` ships with the FileSystem publish, so it deploys with this batch. **Status flips to "fixed locally — pending deploy + prod re-probe."** Post-deploy: `curl -sI https://gccwebapp.com/ | grep -ci permissions-policy` → expect 1 (was 2).

**Date:** 2026-06-02 | **Status:** Fixed locally (web.config dedup in tree) — pending deploy + prod header re-probe | **Severity:** Low (security-header hygiene; no functional impact, but trips header-correctness scanners) | **QC Ref:** internal — follow-up to **DEF-107** | **Reporter:** Governance sweep 2026-06-02 (promoted from the 2026-05-21 status-sync "🔴 STILL FAILING" flag)

**Why this is a new DEF, not just a DEF-107 note.** DEF-107 was recorded as fixed and shipped, but the 2026-05-21 targeted-probe sweep (`qc159-live-check/older-defs-grouped-sweep.js`) found the `Permissions-Policy` header **back to count=2** on gccwebapp.com. A fix that was marked shipped but is observably failing on prod needs its own open tracking item so it doesn't get lost inside a closed entry. DEF-107 stays closed-as-shipped for the original fix; DEF-235 owns the regression.

**Likely root cause (to confirm).** Two independent injection points are both emitting the header — the strong candidate is the same dual-source pattern proven in DEF-135: the IIS-level `web.config` (`<customHeaders>`) **and** the app's security-headers middleware both add `Permissions-Policy`, and unlike CSP (which browsers intersect) duplicate `Permissions-Policy` headers are simply both sent. Browsers honor the first; scanners flag the dupe.

**Reinvestigation plan (not yet run — logged only this session):**
1. `curl -sI https://gccwebapp.com/ | findstr /I "permissions-policy"` — confirm count=2 still reproduces.
2. Grep both sources: `web.config` `<httpProtocol><customHeaders>` and the middleware that sets security headers (the same place DEF-135's CSP lives). Identify which two are emitting it.
3. Fix by removing the header from one source (prefer middleware-only, consistent with the DEF-135 "consolidate to middleware" architecture note) — or have the middleware `Remove` before `Add` so it's idempotent regardless of what web.config sent.
4. Post-deploy: re-run the prod smoke header assertion to confirm count=1.

### DEF-299 — SearchableSelect drops typed value unless a row is mouse-clicked → Create cert fails "Certification Type: the value '' is invalid"

**Date:** 2026-06-25 | **Status:** Fixed locally (`wwwroot/js/searchable-select.js`) — deployed 2026-06-26 | **Severity:** High (blocks the core Create-certificate flow for the most common selection gesture) | **QC Ref:** internal — live report during Create-cert testing | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-06-25)

**Symptom.** On `/Certificate/Create`, selecting a Certification Type then saving threw a validation error: *"Certification Type — the value is invalid."* Reproduced reliably even though a type was visibly chosen.

**Root cause.** `Certification Type` (and other fields) use the `SearchableSelect` type-ahead widget, which hides the native `<select>` and drives it from a text input. The widget only wrote the value back to the underlying `<select>` when the user **clicked a dropdown row with the mouse**. The three keyboard/blur gestures all left the `<select>` empty:

| Gesture | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Click option | ✅ commits | ✅ |
| Type name + Enter | ❌ empty | ✅ |
| Type name + Tab | ❌ empty | ✅ |
| Type name + click away | ❌ empty | ✅ |

`CertificationTypeId` is a `[Required]` non-nullable `int`, so an empty post produces ASP.NET's model-binding message *"The value '' is invalid."* (not the friendlier controller guard). Most users type-then-Enter, so they hit this constantly.

**Fix.** Added `commitTypedValue()` to `SearchableSelect`: on Enter (when no row is arrow-highlighted), Tab, and click-away, the typed text commits to the `<select>` when it resolves to a single option (exact case-insensitive match, or a unique partial match). Ambiguous/no-match text still commits nothing (forces an explicit pick) — no risk of selecting the wrong option. This is a shared-component fix, so it corrects the same trap on every `SearchableSelect`-wrapped field (Certification Type, Product Category, etc.).

**Verification.** `Scripts/smoke-prod/_certtype-gesture-repro.js` (localhost, analyst) — all four gestures now set `select.value`; before the fix only the mouse-click did.

**Cross-ref:** component shared with the Product Category cascade. Relates to the DEF-185 class (non-nullable FK guards) — the guard message is friendlier, but the real bug here was the empty post, not the message.

### DEF-300 — Certificate CSV import: overwriting existing certs is impossible from the Internal tile view (overwrite-acknowledgement guard dead-ends as an error)

**Date:** 2026-06-25 | **Status:** Fixed locally (`Views/Certificate/CertificateTileViewInternal.cshtml`) — pending deploy | **Severity:** High (blocks re-importing / updating any existing certificate via the Internal tile-view import modal) | **QC Ref:** internal — live report during import testing | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-06-25)

**Symptom.** On `/Certificate/CertificateTileViewInternal`, importing a CSV that matches existing certificates: preview reported "0 new, 5 updated", the analyst clicked **Apply Import** on the Confirm dialog, and the modal then showed a red **Error** dialog — *"Import failed: 5 existing certificate(s) would be overwritten. Acknowledge to proceed — a backup of their current data is saved automatically first."* — with only an **OK** button. Clicking OK looped back to Confirm → Apply → same error, with no way to ever proceed. Reported as "it kinda works to overwrite after the analyst agrees but then fails anyway."

**Root cause.** Front-end gap, not a server/DB failure. The server's `ApiApply` (CR-023 R5 overwrite guard, `Controllers/CertificateImportController.cs`) is working as designed: when overwrites are pending and not yet acknowledged it returns a 400 with `requiresOverwriteAck: true` + `overwriteCount` so the **client** can prompt and re-submit with `acknowledgeOverwrites: true` (same pattern for `requiresReassignmentAck`). The import modal's `applyBtn` handler in `CertificateTileViewInternal.cshtml` posted `{ importId }` with **no acknowledgement flags** and treated any non-success response as `throw new Error(result.message)` — so the guard message rendered as a terminal error with no acknowledge-and-retry path. The full-page MVC flow (`Views/CertificateImport/Preview.cshtml`) already handles this via server-rendered ack checkboxes; only the modal path was broken.

**Fix.** Extracted the apply call into a retryable `applyImport(acks)` function. On a `requiresReassignmentAck` or `requiresOverwriteAck` response it shows an `AdminCore.showConfirmation` (`type: 'danger'`) explaining the consequence (and the automatic backup), and on confirm re-calls `applyImport()` with the matching flag set true — accumulating both acks if the server requests them in sequence (reassignment is checked before overwrite server-side). Success toast now also notes the backup count when one was taken.

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED on localhost (2026-06-25) via `Scripts/smoke-prod/def300-import-overwrite-verify.js` — ALL PASS. The smoke exports one existing cert, tweaks its Location to force a Modified/overwrite row, drives the real modal (open → upload → preview shows 1 modified → Apply → Confirm → **"Overwrite existing certificate(s)?" prompt appears** → confirm), and asserts the two API calls: first `/api/CertificateImport/Apply` returns `requiresOverwriteAck:true` (overwriteCount 1), second returns `success:true, certificatesUpdated:1, backupCertificateCount:1`; the new Location is then confirmed persisted via re-export. (User also has the pre-fix dead-end loop screenshots: `Screenshot_25-6-2026_1519*–1520*`.)

**Follow-ups observed while tracing (NOT part of this fix — logged for triage):**
1. **Identical re-imports are flagged "Modified" when a cert has internal tags.** `DetectChanges` (`CertificateImportService.cs`) compares the cert's existing tags (internal **and** external) against the CSV's external-tag column only, so any cert carrying an internal tag always shows as changed on a clean round-trip — which is why a re-import of unchanged data even triggers the overwrite prompt.
2. **An applied overwrite drops internal tags.** `UpdateCertificateAsync` does `Tags.Clear()` then re-adds external tags only, so overwriting silently removes internal tags. Both (1) and (2) warrant their own DEF once confirmed.

**Cross-ref:** server contract intentionally unchanged (guard + auto-backup are correct). Same modal lives only in the Internal tile view; External has no import.

### DEF-301 — Company names (or any query value) containing an apostrophe/quote fail to load: SQL-injection middleware false-positives on URL-encoded `%27`/`%22`

**Date:** 2026-07-01 | **Status:** Fixed (`Middleware/SecurityHeadersMiddleware.cs`) — **bundled in `GCCWebApp-deploy-20260701-1639.zip`**, pending deploy | **Severity:** High (any certificate whose company name contains an apostrophe — e.g. `Gemma's Company Co.`, `O'Brien` — cannot be filtered/viewed in the tile views; also blocks search terms and autocomplete carrying `'` or `"`) | **QC Ref:** internal — live report during tile-view filter testing | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-07-01)

**Symptom.** Filtering the certificate tile views by a company whose name contains an apostrophe (e.g. `Gemma's Company Co.`) shows the red **"Failed to load certificates"** error and no tiles render. Reported as a "URL encoding issue with `'` → `%27`."

**Root cause.** Server-side, **not** a client encoding bug. The tile JS is correct — `buildApiParams()` uses `URLSearchParams`, which properly encodes `'` → `%27`. The failure is in `SecurityHeadersMiddleware.DetectSqlInjectionAsync`: it inspected `context.Request.QueryString.ToString()`, which returns the **still-URL-encoded** query string, and its pattern list contained the bare tokens `%27` and `%22`. So a filter like `company=Gemma%27s%20Company%20Co.` matched the "SQL injection" signature → middleware short-circuited with **HTTP 400 "Bad request"** → the tile `fetch` failed → the UI surfaced "Failed to load certificates." Because the check was on the raw query string, this hit **every** query parameter carrying a legitimate apostrophe or double-quote (company/search/autocomplete), not just company names.

**Fix.** In `DetectSqlInjectionAsync`, decode the query string before matching (`Uri.UnescapeDataString`, with `+`→space) and drop the standalone `%27`/`%22` (and now-redundant `%3b%20drop`/`%3b%20delete`) tokens from the query pattern list. Detection now runs against actual values, so the meaningful injection combinations (`' or `, `'; drop`, `'--`, `union select`, …) still fire — and in fact now work against decoded input where the encoded-only matching had been largely inert — while an ordinary lone apostrophe/quote passes. `pathInjectionPatterns` left untouched (`Request.Path` is already framework-decoded; company values never travel in the path).

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED on localhost:5101 (2026-07-01) via `curl` against `/api/certificate-tiles`: `company=Gemma%27s%20Company%20Co.` → **HTTP 200** (was 400 pre-fix); `search=O%27Brien` → **200**; plain control → **200**; real injection `company=x%27 OR %271%27%3D%271` → **400** (still blocked); `search=1 union select password from users` → **400** (still blocked). Legitimate apostrophes load; genuine injection payloads remain rejected.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_client_requested_labels_immutable]] (data/behavior fix, not a copy change), [[feedback_scoping_check_adjacent_endpoints]] (verified the same middleware guards all three tile APIs + autocomplete, not just the reported one).

### DEF-302 — Certificate tile views flash a misleading "0 Results" before the first load resolves (search reads as "nothing found")

**Date:** 2026-07-01 | **Status:** Fixed (3 views `Views/Certificate/CertificateTileView*.cshtml` + 3 scripts `wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view*.js`) — **bundled in `GCCWebApp-deploy-20260701-1639.zip`**, pending deploy | **Severity:** Low — UX polish. Search is functionally correct (a free-text query returns the right rows); the count area just momentarily reads "0 Results" during the fetch, which looks like "no matches found." | **QC Ref:** internal — live report during search testing | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-07-01)

**Symptom.** On the certificate tile views, running a free-text search (e.g. "Recycled") correctly returns the matching certificates, but on the initial render the results count briefly shows **"0 Results"** before the tiles load — reading as "nothing found" for a beat even though matches are on the way.

**Root cause.** Pure front-end placeholder, not a search bug. The results-count element was hardcoded in the Razor markup as `<div id="resultsCount">0 Results</div>`. The count is only corrected by `updateResultsCount()` **after** the async `/api/certificate-tiles` fetch resolves (`Showing N of N …`), so during the initial load window — page load, a hard nav to a `?search=…` URL, or any first fetch — the static "0 Results" is what shows. `showLoadingIndicator()` puts a spinner in the grid, but the count line still contradicted it by asserting zero.

**Fix.** Two parts: **(1) Initial render** — changed the static placeholder in all three tile views from `0 Results` to a neutral **`Loading…`**, so the first paint never asserts "zero matches" before data arrives. **(2) Every re-search / filter change** (per Shawn 2026-07-01) — in each tile view's `loadCertificates(append)`, on a fresh (`!append`) load the count is now reset to `Loading…` **synchronously, before the `await fetch`**, so a subsequent search/filter no longer leaves the stale prior "Showing N of N" up during the new fetch either. In both cases `updateResultsCount()` overwrites it with the real "Showing N of N certificates" on fetch success exactly as before. Markup + JS only, **no API/migration change**; the three scripts already carry `asp-append-version="true"` (DEF-271) so the JS change cache-busts on deploy. (The public view's `resultsCount` carries `aria-live="polite"`, so this also stops a screen reader from ever seeing a "0 Results" value.)

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED on localhost:5101 (2026-07-01): the public tile page now server-renders `id="resultsCount" …>Loading…</div>` and `grep` finds **zero** `>0 Results<` occurrences; a `search=Recycled` query against `/api/certificate-tiles` returns `totalCount=4` (dev-seed data set — client env had 7), confirming the filter itself is unaffected. Internal/External carry the identical markup change (both require auth, so unauthenticated curl returns the login redirect; source-string replacement confirmed in each file). JS extension: `node --check` clean on all three scripts, and the reset is placed synchronously ahead of the `await` so the "Loading…" state is deterministic on every fresh load (the flip back to "Showing N" is sub-second, so not separately screenshotted).

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_no_chaos_rabbit_holes]] (single-cause markup fix, no over-diagnosis), [[feedback_client_requested_labels_immutable]] (label swap is a loading-state correction, not a client-requested copy change).

### DEF-303 — Certificate tile-view search fired while typing (300 ms debounce) instead of on submit; the active-filter chip ("tag") was drawn before the user pressed Enter

**Date:** 2026-07-13 | **Status:** Fixed (3 scripts `wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view*.js`) — working tree, **pending next deploy bundle** | **Severity:** Low/Medium — UX. Search was functional, but committed itself prematurely: after a typing pause the query ran, the results reloaded, the URL rewrote, and a filter chip appeared before the user had finished/submitted. | **QC Ref:** internal — client discussion on the tile-view search (public/internal/external) | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-07-13, relaying client)

**Symptom.** On all three certificate tile views, the client observed that "when someone starts to search, the tag gets set before Enter is clicked." Typing a few characters and pausing caused a search-term **filter chip** to appear above the results (in `#activeFilterTags`) and the grid to reload — with no Enter press and no suggestion selected.

**Root cause.** The search box committed on a **300 ms debounce of the `input` event**, not on submit. In each tile script's `initializeAutocomplete()`, the `input` handler ran `setTimeout(() => { state.filters.search = term; renderActiveFilterTags(); updateUrl(); loadInitialCertificates(); }, 300)`. So after a brief typing pause the code set the search filter, **drew the chip**, rewrote the URL, and reloaded results — all before the user submitted. A proper Enter (`keydown`) handler and an autocomplete-click handler already existed and did the same commit, making the debounced auto-commit redundant with the real submit paths. (Checkbox filters were never affected — they apply on click only.)

**Fix.** Removed the debounced search-commit from the `input` handler in all three scripts, leaving `input` to drive **only** the autocomplete dropdown. Because the debounce used to be what drew the chip during typing, the two real commit paths never called `renderActiveFilterTags()` themselves — so added it to (1) the Enter handler (both the typed-text and selected-suggestion branches) and (2) the autocomplete-click handler, so the chip now appears exactly on submit. Also collapsed the Enter handler's `else if (value.trim())` into an `else` that commits the trimmed value including empty, so **clearing the box + Enter now removes an active search** (previously only the chip's × cleared it, since live-search backspacing was gone). JS only — **no `.cshtml`, API, or migration change**; the three scripts already carry `asp-append-version` (DEF-271) so they cache-bust on deploy. Vestigial `clearTimeout(state.debounceTimer)` calls left in place as harmless no-ops rather than make unrelated edits.

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED on localhost:5101 (2026-07-13) via Playwright across **all three views** (public unauthenticated; internal/external as analyst `jane.analyst@anukiconsulting.com` against the seeded `GCCDatabase_Dev`). Per view: typing `cert` and waiting >1 s (past the old 300 ms) → **chips=0, result-reloads=0** (was: chip + reload); pressing Enter → **chip=1, reload=1**; clearing + Enter → **chip=0**. Autocomplete still functions (dropdown shows 5/11/9 suggestions on the three views) and **zero console errors**. `node --check` clean on all three scripts. Files: `wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view.js`, `certificate-tile-view-internal.js`, `certificate-tile-view-external.js`.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_client_requested_labels_immutable]] (behavior fix, no copy change), [[feedback_scoping_check_adjacent_endpoints]] (same handler fixed identically across all three tile scripts, not just the one first noticed), [[feedback_testing_environment]] (verified on localhost, seeded dev DB), [[feedback_playwright_screenshots]] (Playwright validation across views).

### DEF-304 — Shareable-URL filters only half-wired on the Internal & External tile views: sidebar filter selections (type/category/company/country/tags) weren't added to the URL, so a shared link dropped them

**Date:** 2026-07-13 | **Status:** Fixed (2 scripts `wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view-internal.js`, `-external.js`) — working tree, **pending next deploy bundle** | **Severity:** Medium — the client relies on sharing a filtered tile-view link; on the authed views the link lost every sidebar filter, silently showing the recipient a different (broader) result set. | **QC Ref:** internal — client request during external-view search testing | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-07-13, relaying client)

**Symptom.** On `/Certificate/CertificateTileViewExternal` (and Internal), checking a sidebar filter such as `Vantage Vinyl Verified` or `Carbon footprint` filtered the results correctly but **did not appear in the address bar** — the URL stayed at just `?search=…`. Sharing that link reopened the page without those filters. Client asked that "all filters" be appended to the URL so a shared link loads with them applied.

**Root cause.** Feature-parity gap, not a search bug. The **public** view (`certificate-tile-view.js`) already implements full shareable filtered URLs — `updateUrl()` writes every dimension, `setupUrlParameters()` reads them, `restoreFilterCheckboxes()` re-checks the boxes after options load. The **internal** and **external** views were only half-wired: their `updateUrl()` persisted just `search` / `status` / `partner` (with a literal `// ... other parameters` stub), and `setupUrlParameters()` / `restoreFilterCheckboxes()` only handled that same subset. So certType / productCategory / company / country / tags (and non-default sort) were applied to the API call via `buildApiParams()` but never round-tripped through the URL. "Shareable URLs" had been marked complete but only the public view fully implemented it.

**Fix.** Brought internal + external to parity with the public reference (no new design): (1) `updateUrl()` now also writes `certType`, `category`, `company`, `country`, `tags`, and `sort` (sort only when non-default `'newest'`), replacing the stub; (2) `setupUrlParameters()` parses those same params into `state.filters`; (3) `restoreFilterCheckboxes()` re-checks the matching boxes via the existing `updateCheckboxes(name, values)` helper (`cert-type`/`product-cat`/`company`/`countries`/`additional`) after the async options populate. URL param names + checkbox `name`s were taken from each file's own `handleFilterChange` `filterMap` (tags ↔ `additional`). `updateCheckboxes` only sets `.checked` — it does not mutate `state.filters` — so no double-counting on restore. JS only, **no `.cshtml`/API/migration change**; scripts carry `asp-append-version` (cache-busts on deploy). Public view untouched (already correct).

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED on localhost:5101 (2026-07-13) via Playwright on **both** authed views (analyst login), using the client's own filter: applied `certType="+Vantage Vinyl Verified"` + `company="3M"` → URL became `?certType=%2BVantage+Vinyl+Verified&company=3M`; loading that URL **fresh in a new page** re-checked both boxes and rendered **2 active filter chips**, with results scoped. `node --check` clean on all three scripts. ### DEF-305 — Certificate Edit: a rejected workflow-status change traps the form (invalid choice stays selected → blind re-save fails again) and the error doesn't say which statuses ARE allowed

> **SUPERSEDED by CR-028 (2026-07-20):** the client decided to **remove the transition matrix** entirely — status is now freely selectable, so there is no longer any rejection path to trap the user. This DEF's fix (dropdown snap-back + allowed-next-states message) is now moot; the rejection block it improved was deleted. Kept for history. See change-request register CR-028.

**Date:** 2026-07-13 | **Status:** ~~Fixed~~ **Superseded by CR-028** (`Controllers/CertificateController.cs`, `Models/CertificateStatus.cs`) — the rejection path was removed, not just improved | **Severity:** Medium — usability; the workflow rules are correct but a user who picks a disallowed status gets stuck and cannot tell how to proceed. | **QC Ref:** internal — client observation | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-07-13, relaying client), while editing a cert from Draft → Republished

**Symptom.** The client set a Draft cert's Status to **Republished**, save was rejected with *"Invalid status transition from 'Draft' to 'Republished'. Check workflow rules for the allowed next states…"*, and then reported he **could not re-save or recreate**. The transition matrix (DEF-203, added 2026-05-19) is behaving correctly — Draft → Republished is genuinely disallowed — so this is a UX defect, **not** a rules defect. Explicitly scoped: the rules were left unchanged; a separate sign-off doc (`docs/tracking/certificate-status-transition-matrix.md`) captures the matrix for client verification.

**Root cause.** Two gaps in the rejection path at `CertificateController.cs` Edit POST: (1) on rejection the code re-rendered `View(model)` **without resetting `model.Status`**, so the Status `<select>` (which selects on `Model.Status`, `Views/Certificate/Edit.cshtml:185`) redisplayed the *invalid* choice — a blind re-save re-submitted the same bad value and failed identically, reading as a lock-out; nothing had actually persisted (the cert kept its true stored status). (2) The error told the user to "check workflow rules" but never listed the allowed next states, so they had to guess.

**Fix.** (1) Snap the field back to the certificate's true stored status. **Note (found during validation):** `model.Status = oldStatus` **alone is not enough** — the `<select asp-for="Status">` tag helper binds to ModelState's *posted* value, which overrides the model property on re-render, so the dropdown kept showing "Republished." The working fix also calls `ModelState.Remove(nameof(model.Status))` (to drop the stale posted value) **then** re-adds the transition error to that key so the message still renders against the field. (2) New helper `CertificateStatusHelper.GetAllowedNextStatusDisplayNames(fromStatus)` (`Models/CertificateStatus.cs`) enumerates the matrix and the error now appends *"From '{from}' you can move to: {list}."* (or "…is a final state…" when empty). No change to the transition matrix, roles, or any other save path; the DEF-171/285 auto-expire bypasses are untouched. C# only — no view/API/migration change. Build clean (0 errors).

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED on localhost:5101 (2026-07-13) via Playwright (admin login) against seeded Draft fixture `99-9001`. **7/7 GREEN:** edit form loads with stored status Draft → pick Republished → save → (a) error banner shows *"Invalid status transition from 'Draft' to 'Republished'. From 'Draft' you can move to: Client Approved - Not Paid, Client Approved - Confidential, Client Approved - Paid, Hold."*, (b) Status dropdown **snapped back to Draft** (the trap), (c) a straight re-save then **succeeded and left the Edit page** (redirect to the internal detail view) — proving the lock-out is gone. Screenshots in `Scripts/smoke-prod/_results/def305/`. First pass caught the ModelState-binding gap above (dropdown stuck on Republished); re-verified GREEN after the `ModelState.Remove` fix + rebuild. Fixtures torn down; app stopped.

**Linked memory.** DEF-203 (the transition matrix this makes usable), [[feedback_client_requested_labels_immutable]] (behavior/UX fix, copy driven by rules not invented), `docs/tracking/certificate-status-transition-matrix.md` (companion sign-off spec — rules left for client to verify).

### DEF-306 — Certificate CSV export: values starting with + = - @ (e.g. "+Vantage Vinyl Verified" cert type) render as #NAME? in Excel (CSV formula injection)

**Date:** 2026-07-17 | **Status:** Fixed (`Services/CertificateService.cs`, `Controllers/ExportController.cs`, `wwwroot/js/admin/exportUtils.js`, `Services/ProductIdService.cs`, `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js`) — working tree, **pending next deploy bundle** | **Severity:** Medium — data-quality / cosmetic in the export, but also a latent CSV-injection vector. | **QC Ref:** internal — client observation | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-07-17, relaying client), on the "Export database to CSV" file

**Symptom.** In the exported certificate CSV, the certification type **"+Vantage Vinyl Verified"** shows in the Certification Type cell as **`#NAME?`**; opening the cell reveals Excel has treated it as the formula `=+Vantage Vinyl Verified`. Affects any cell whose value begins with a formula-trigger character (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`).

**Root cause.** `CertificateService.GenerateCsvExport` wrapped every field in quotes but `EscapeCsvField` only doubled embedded quotes — it did nothing about leading formula-trigger characters. RFC-4180 quoting does **not** stop Excel/Sheets from evaluating a quoted cell as a formula, so `+Vantage Vinyl Verified` was parsed as a formula → `#NAME?`.

**Fix.** New `CsvCell()` helper builds each text cell: normal values stay RFC-4180 quoted (`"value"`); values starting with `= + - @` or a leading tab/CR are emitted in **Excel text format** (`="value"`), which displays literally, cannot execute, and is the **same wrapper the importer already unwraps** via `StripExcelTextFormat` (applied to every column in `GetFieldWithMapping`) — so an exported file re-imports losslessly. All text emissions in `GenerateCsvExport` routed through `CsvCell` (date columns left as plain quoted literals — they can't be formulas). No change to the export's columns, ordering, role-gating (DEF-295/247/198), the Amazon partner API, or any migration. C# only; build clean (0 compile errors — output-copy step was blocked only because the dev app was running).

**Scope.** All three CSV export surfaces were fixed in one batch (Shawn asked to resolve the other instances too): (1) the main certificate export `CertificateService.GenerateCsvExport` (new `CsvCell` helper); (2) the dashboard/report CSV builders in `Controllers/ExportController.cs` — `CsvField` now neutralises formulas and `GenerateStatCsv` / `GenerateCertificateReportCsv` / `GenerateTableCsv` were routed through it; (3) the admin client-side exporter `wwwroot/js/admin/exportUtils.js` (`exportToCSV`). The Excel builders (ClosedXML, `GenerateStatExcel` etc.) don't need it — ClosedXML writes typed cells, not formula-parsed text.

**Added hardening (same batch, Shawn 2026-07-17): leading-zero-safe identifier columns.** The ASIN/UPC/GTIN/EAN columns in the certificate export now always emit Excel text format via a new `CsvTextCell` helper (non-empty → `="value"`, empty → `""`), so Excel no longer silently converts a code like UPC `012345678905` to the number `12345678905` / strips leading zeros. Same `="value"` wrapper as the formula fix, so round-trip via `StripExcelTextFormat` stays lossless. Scoped to those four columns in `GenerateCsvExport`.

**Extended to `ProductIdValue` (Shawn 2026-07-17).** Both product-ID exports now emit the identifier value in Excel text format: (a) `ExportController.DownloadActiveProductIds` — new `CsvTextField` for the "Product ID/ID Value" column; (b) `ProductIdService.ExportToCsvAsync` (the per-cert Product ID Manager export at `GET /api/productids/certificate/{id}/export`) — this method had **no escaping at all** (raw `"{value}"`, so a quote/comma in ProductName/Description could corrupt a row and a `+`-leading value ran as a formula); rewrote it to route every field through new `CsvCell`/`CsvTextCell` helpers, with `ProductIdValue` via `CsvTextCell`. **Round-trip:** the product-ID import parser (`product-id-manager.js`) does NOT go through the certificate importer's `StripExcelTextFormat`, and its `parseCSVLine` mangles `="12345"` into `=12345`; added a JS `stripExcelTextFormat` helper (handles both the intact `="…"` and the stray-leading-`=` residue) applied to the value + SKU on import, so a raw re-import of an exported file is lossless. Text format also *removes* the reason `fixScientificNotation` existed — Excel now keeps these as text, so long UPCs/GTINs no longer degrade to `1.23E+11`.

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED live on localhost:5101 (2026-07-17), dev DB `GCCDatabase_Dev` which contains the exact cert type `+Vantage Vinyl Verified` (Id 24, used by cert `26-0175`, Client Approved - Paid). (a) Anonymous `GET /Certificate/ExportCertificates` → Certification Type cell = `="+Vantage Vinyl Verified"` (was raw `+Vantage…`); normal values (`"Client Approved - Paid"`, `"Gemma's Company Co.®"`) stay plain-quoted. (b) **Analyst-authenticated** cert export (27-col internal path, `includeInternalTags`) → same `="+Vantage Vinyl Verified"`. (c) `ExportController` — analyst `GET /Export/DownloadStat?type=product-categories-with-active-certs` → `…,="+Vantage Vinyl Verified",…` via the fixed `CsvField`. (d) `exportUtils.js` branch checked with an 8-case Node harness — all pass, incl. edge cases (leading-hyphen only triggers when first char; commas still quote; embedded quotes escape). Exported format `="value"` matches `StripExcelTextFormat` exactly, so re-import is lossless (verified by code, not re-run to avoid DB writes). `dotnet build` clean (0 errors). (e) **Leading-zero identifiers** verified live with a temporary fixture on `26-0175` (dev DB): set ASIN=`0ABCDEF123`, UPC=`012345678905`, GTIN=`00012345678905`, EAN=`0075678164125`, re-exported → all four emitted as `="…"` with leading zeros intact; **fixture fully reverted** afterwards (all four back to NULL, matching the row's original empty state — External Tag `APR` untouched). Note: `26-0175`'s pre-mutation identifier state wasn't captured before editing; restored to NULL (functionally identical to empty in-app), confirmed by re-export matching the original row byte-for-byte.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_track_every_fix_in_defect_register]], [[feedback_client_requested_labels_immutable]] (data untouched — only the Excel encoding changed, the label stays "+Vantage Vinyl Verified").

### DEF-307 — Certificate CSV export: non-ASCII characters (e.g. right single quote ' in a product name) render as mojibake "â€™" in Excel (missing UTF-8 BOM)

**Date:** 2026-07-17 | **Status:** Fixed (`Extensions/CsvExportHelper.cs` [new], `Controllers/CertificateController.cs`, `Controllers/ExportController.cs`, `Controllers/DashboardController.cs`) — working tree, **pending next deploy bundle** | **Severity:** Medium — cosmetic corruption of exported text, but garbles any product/company name with a smart-quote, em dash, or accent. | **QC Ref:** internal — client observation | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-07-17, relaying client), on the "Export database to CSV" file, cert `26-0161`

**Symptom.** Exporting the certificate database to CSV, a product name containing a right single quotation mark — `Testing Very Very Long Product Name That's Over 100 Characters…` (the `'` is U+2019, not a plain ASCII apostrophe) — opens in Excel as `…That**â€™**s Over 100 Characters…`. (Sibling to DEF-306, same "Export database to CSV" file, adjacent cert.)

**Root cause.** The certificate export (`CertificateService.GenerateCsvExport`) and the dashboard/report/table exports (`ExportController`, `DashboardController`) returned `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(csv)` — correct UTF-8 bytes but with **no byte-order mark**. Excel on Windows decodes a BOM-less CSV as its Windows-1252 default, so the three UTF-8 bytes of `'` (`E2 80 99`) are shown as the Latin-1 glyphs `â € ™`. Same class of bug already fixed for the *import template* (`CertificateImportController.DownloadTemplate`, em dash `â€"`) — that fix prepended the UTF-8 BOM; the export paths never got the same treatment. (The user's pasted "actual" text also showed some transposition — `VeVery…'ry` — which is a copy-artifact of hand-copying the garbled Excel cell; the single defect is the encoding, and the BOM resolves what renders.)

**Fix.** New shared helper `Extensions/CsvExportHelper.cs` — `ToCsvBytesWithBom(string)` and `WithBom(byte[])`, both using `new UTF8Encoding(encoderShouldEmitUTF8Identifier: true)` and prepending the BOM (matching the existing `CertificateImportController` idiom). Applied at the **MVC/browser download return sites** only:
- `CertificateController.ExportCertificates` (the reported "Export database" download) → `WithBom(exportData)`.
- `ExportController` — all four CSV returns (`DownloadStat`, `DownloadReport`, `DownloadTable`, `DownloadActiveProductIds`).
- `DashboardController` — all three CSV returns (`DownloadStat` aggregate + detail, `DownloadTable`).

**Scope / what was deliberately NOT touched.** The BOM is added at the MVC controller, **not** inside the shared `CertificateService.ExportCertificatesAsync`/`GenerateCsvExport`, because that same method feeds the frozen **`/api/v1/certificates/export` Amazon partner API** (`CertificatesApiController`). Adding a BOM there would change the contract bytes a machine consumer parses — out of scope without partner sign-off ([[feedback_amazon_api_immutable]]). So the analyst browser download is fixed while the partner API export stays byte-identical. No column, ordering, role-gating, data, or migration change. C# only; compiles clean (the 2 build errors were the output-copy step blocked by the running dev app, not compilation).

**Verification.** Code-level: helper emits `EF BB BF` preamble + UTF-8 body; partner API path (`CertificatesApiController`) confirmed to bypass the helper. Live re-export verification against dev DB pending (dev app holding the exe lock at time of fix).

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_track_every_fix_in_defect_register]], [[feedback_amazon_api_immutable]], [[feedback_client_requested_labels_immutable]] (data untouched — only the file encoding changed).

### DEF-308 — Certificate Create: PDF preview shows a broken-image link before save (Edit shows it fine)

**Date:** 2026-07-17 | **Status:** Fixed (`Program.cs`) — working tree, **pending next deploy bundle** | **Severity:** Medium — cosmetic-but-alarming: the pre-save thumbnail preview on the Create form never renders, so an analyst uploading a PDF sees a broken-image icon and can't confirm the correct file/page was attached until after saving. No data loss (the PDF still uploads and the thumbnail still generates and persists). | **QC Ref:** internal — client observation | **Reporter:** Shawn (2026-07-17, relaying client "CP NOTE"), on the Certificate Creation page: *"Cert preview after uploading PDF shows broken link… when you create and upload before saving that this happens. After I saved and returned to edit it did appear."*

**Symptom.** On `/Certificate/Create`, after uploading a PDF the sidebar "Certificate Preview" briefly shows "Generating preview…" then renders a **broken-image icon**. The exact same certificate, reopened in Edit after save, shows the thumbnail correctly.

**Root cause.** A route-parameter-name mismatch. On upload, `wwwroot/js/certificate-create.js` POSTs the PDF to `api/CertificatesApi/GenerateThumbnail`, which generates the PNG and returns `thumbnailUrl = "/Certificate/PreviewThumbnail/{fileName}"` (DEF-208 pre-save flow — the cert has no Id yet, so it can't route through `ViewCertificateImage/{id}`). The JS sets that URL as the `<img src>`. But `CertificateController.PreviewThumbnail(string fileName)` was reached only through the **default conventional route** `{controller}/{action}/{id?}`, whose trailing token is named **`id`**, not `fileName`. ASP.NET model binding is by name, so the `{fileName}` segment bound to `id` and the action's `fileName` parameter stayed **null** → the guard `string.IsNullOrEmpty(fileName)` returned `NotFound()` → broken image. Edit worked because `ViewCertificateImage(int id)` binds the `{id}` token correctly. The endpoint essentially never rendered a live preview on Create.

**Fix.** Added an explicit `MapControllerRoute` in `Program.cs` — `pattern: "Certificate/PreviewThumbnail/{fileName}"` mapped to `Certificate/PreviewThumbnail`, placed **before** the default route — mirroring the app's existing convention for non-`id` route params (the `Certificate/Edit/{number}` and `Certificate/Delete/{number}` explicit routes). The `{fileName}` segment now binds to the action parameter. No controller/view/JS/service/API/migration change; the action's own traversal sanitization (`..`, `/`, `\` → `NotFound`) and `AnalystOrAdmin` gate are untouched. Build clean (0 errors).

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED live on localhost:5101 (2026-07-17). After rebuild + restart, authenticated as analyst (`jane.analyst@anukiconsulting.com`) and requested the exact broken route against a real existing thumbnail: `GET /Certificate/PreviewThumbnail/26-0023_thumb_20260612_185805.png` → **200, PNG rendered** (Chrome reported `464×600`, the "GCC Local Thumbnail Test" thumbnail displayed). Pre-fix this same route returned the broken-image 404 (root cause confirmed by the `{id}` vs `fileName` binding above). Full browser create-upload flow was not re-driven because the session's `file_upload` no longer accepts host paths, but the failing hop was the `<img src>` GET, which this test exercises directly.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_track_every_fix_in_defect_register]], [[feedback_def_entries_note_qc_id]], [[feedback_no_chaos_rabbit_holes]] (root-caused in code before touching the browser). DEF-208 (the pre-save thumbnail flow this route serves).

**Follow-up — client 2026-07-20 (zoom manifestation, RESOLVED — no separate DEF).** The client re-reported the same underlying issue from a different control, on the Certificate Creation page: *"When clicking 'zoom' on cert preview, opens a blank page with no PDF. …Maybe you have to save the cert before these things work?"* (Reporter: client via Shawn.) **Same root cause as this DEF:** the zoom modal (`openImageZoom()` in `Views/Certificate/Create.cshtml`) loads the **same** `/Certificate/PreviewThumbnail/{fileName}` image as the inline sidebar preview — so pre-save, before the DEF-308 route fix deploys, it is blank for the identical `{id}`-vs-`fileName` binding reason (and the zoom shows a full-size image snapshot, never the PDF — consistent with Edit/Detail/Tile; no PDF viewer exists in the app and Requirements.md is silent on one). **Disposition (Shawn, 2026-07-20): resolved — working as designed; the certificate preview and its zoom are available after the certificate is saved.** No new code and no new DEF number (Question bucket, not a distinct bug); the pre-save case is carried by DEF-308's routing fix in the next deploy bundle. Logged in `observations_log.md` + `shipped-2026-07.md` (2026-07-20). ⚠️ **Post-deploy note:** once DEF-308 ships, the pre-save preview/zoom *will* render on Create, so the client-facing "only works after save" wording should be retired at that point.

### DEF-309 — Certificates: rapid sort/filter changes silently dropped (data disagrees with the Sort-By label/URL)

**Date:** 2026-07-17 (mirror completed 2026-07-19) | **Status:** Fixed (`wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view-internal.js`, `certificate-tile-view-external.js`, `certificate-tile-view.js` — all three tile views) — working tree, **pending next deploy bundle** | **Severity:** Medium — the certificate list can display data sorted differently from what the Sort-By control and `?sort=` URL claim, so an analyst trusts an order that isn't applied. No data loss. | **QC Ref:** internal — client observation (white-screen intake, 2026-07-16) | **Reporter:** client via Shawn — on the Certificates page: *"Sorting by oldest effective date made screen go white but results were still there — clicked on screen and it opened one of the results. Refreshed the blank results page and the certificates showed up."*

**Origin.** Surfaced while investigating the client's "white screen on Oldest Effective Date sort" report. That white-screen symptom (rows present + clickable, self-heals on refresh) is the signature of a stalled compositor paint and **could not be reproduced** in automation — headless OR a real-GPU headed run — across 20 checks at desktop width under 4× CPU throttle (see observations_log.md 2026-07-16, harness `Scripts/smoke-prod/cert-sort-whitescreen-discovery.js`). The investigation did, however, expose this separate, reproducible correctness defect.

**Root cause.** `loadCertificates()` opened with a blanket `if (state.isLoading) return;`. That guard is correct for infinite-scroll *appends* (they must not stack) but it also **dropped a fresh sort/filter/search reload** that arrived while any load was in flight. The sort handler still updated the Sort-By label and pushed `?sort=` to the URL, but the data was never re-fetched — so the visible table stayed on the previous sort while the UI claimed the new one. Confirmed empirically: 4 rapid sort clicks produced only 2 API calls.

**Fix.** Load-sequence token. Only appends still bail on `isLoading` (`if (append && state.isLoading) return;`); a fresh load always proceeds and takes `const seq = ++state.loadSeq`. After the fetch (and again after parsing the body), a stale `seq !== state.loadSeq` result is discarded so a slow earlier response can't overwrite a newer one out of order; the `finally` clears `isLoading`/hides the spinner **only** for the latest seq. Net effect: the most recent sort always wins; no fresh request is ever silently dropped.

**Defensive companion (same change).** Added `nudgeRepaint(el)` — called after every fresh (non-append) render — which forces a reflow + a one-frame `translateZ(0)` toggle on `#gridBody` (list) / `#certificatesGrid` (tile) to defeat a stalled compositor paint (the original white-screen class). Deliberately targets the body/grid **only, never a sticky-header ancestor** — a `transform` on an ancestor of a `position:sticky` element silently breaks the sticky header; `#stickyHeaderRow` is a sibling subtree, so it is unaffected (verified: sticky header renders intact post-fix).

**Scope / not touched.** Applied to all three tile-view scripts: `certificate-tile-view-internal.js` (the reported analyst view), `certificate-tile-view-external.js`, and `certificate-tile-view.js` (public) — **mirrored per Shawn's go-ahead 2026-07-19**. The public file has a distinct retry/backoff load path, so its seq-checks are placed to also skip retry/error handling for a superseded load. No server, API, data, or migration change.

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED on localhost:5101 via `cert-sort-whitescreen-discovery.js` (desktop 1440×900, 4× CPU throttle). Scenario D: fire two different sorts back-to-back, then compare the rendered first-5 certificate numbers against a ground-truth API call for the *last* sort — **PASS, `expected === rendered`, 2 fetches** (pre-fix the 2nd was dropped). No regression: re-sort loop (list+tile), deep-scroll→sort, and background-tab→return all still PASS (21/21); post-fix screenshot confirms sticky header + table render fully with the nudge active. **Mirror (external + public) verified 2026-07-19** via `cert-sort-mirror-verify.js` — initial render, single sort, and rapid double-sort (supersede path) all render with zero page errors on both views (**10/10 PASS**).

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_track_every_fix_in_defect_register]], [[feedback_def_entries_note_qc_id]], [[feedback_no_chaos_rabbit_holes]], [[feedback_playwright_screenshots]].
