### DEF-310 — Edit Certificate: replacing the uploaded document saves correctly but the preview and "View" keep showing the OLD document (browser heuristic caching)

> **Addendum 2026-08-05 — a second, unrelated fix shipped inside this entry and was never written down.** `Services/FileUploadService.cs` (lines 99–101 and 168–170) carries `// DEF-310:` comments describing a *filename* bug: `[0..8]` sat **outside** the interpolation hole, so `$"{…}{Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")}[0..8]{ext}"` wrote the literal characters `[0..8]` into the filename instead of truncating the GUID to 9 chars. Nothing above describes that — this entry is about cache headers — so the register attributes a fix to a defect it never documents, and anyone auditing "what did DEF-310 change?" from the register alone would miss two of its edits.
>
> **Live impact, one row.** Prod has exactly **one** certificate whose stored path still carries the malformed name: **23-0753** → `uploads/certificates/23-0753_20260630_163852_dcc92a9404e04611a4fa07649ea49638[0..8].pdf`, written 2026-06-30, before this fix shipped in the `20260720-1408` bundle. Found while sweeping for missing PDFs; it is one of the 11 currently 404-ing.
>
> **It is not specially recoverable, and the name is not why it 404s.** This entry states plainly that the server side is correct — *"Not a save bug … the new PDF is written under a new timestamped filename … and both DB columns are repointed"* — and square brackets are legal filenames on both Windows and Linux. So a file *was* written under that literal name and has since been lost with the other ten. Per [[feedback_data_issue_vs_defect]] the code is already correct, so the single bad row is **data ops, not a new DEF**.
>
> **Carry into any restore:** the DB path must match the file byte-for-byte, brackets included. Do not "tidy" the filename on the server without updating `Certificates.CertificateFile` in the same step, or a successfully restored file will still 404.

**Date:** 2026-07-20 | **Status:** Fixed (`Controllers/CertificateController.cs`, `Extensions/UploadCacheBusting.cs` (new), `Views/Certificate/Edit.cshtml`, `CertificateSingleView.cshtml`, `CertificateInternalView.cshtml`, `CertificateExternalView.cshtml`, `Views/_ViewImports.cshtml`, `Services/FileUploadService.cs`) — working tree, **pending next deploy bundle** | **Severity:** Medium — no data loss (the correct document IS stored), but an analyst is shown the superseded document and can reasonably conclude the replacement failed, or approve a certificate against the wrong file. | **QC Ref:** QC #191 | **Reporter:** client analyst, corroborated by CP — *"Trying to replace the uploaded document with a new one says it works but still shows the old document in the preview and in the 'view' option further down the page. When I tried to replicate it to see if I missed anything, it worked correctly."* CP note: *"I experienced the same thing. Where it did not work right away (after saving) but when I tried a second time it worked."*

**Root cause.** Not a save bug — the server side is correct. On Edit the new PDF is written under a *new* timestamped filename, the thumbnail is regenerated under a new PNG name, and both DB columns are repointed (`CertificateController.cs:1126-1138`, persisted `:1371`). Nothing is overwritten.

The defect is in **delivery**. All four views render the preview from a stable, un-versioned URL — `/Certificate/ViewCertificateImage/{id}` — and `ViewCertificateImage` / `ViewCertificateFile` returned `PhysicalFile(...)` with **no `Cache-Control` header at all**. Per RFC 9111 a 200 carrying `Last-Modified` but no explicit freshness directive is subject to **heuristic freshness**, conventionally ~10% of the document's age. That is exactly the observed behaviour:

- Replace a document on a certificate whose file was uploaded **weeks ago** → heuristic lifetime of *days* → the browser reuses the cached copy without revalidating. **Stale.**
- Replace on a certificate uploaded **minutes ago** — precisely what you get when you create a test certificate to replicate the issue → heuristic lifetime of *seconds* → revalidates → correct file.

That asymmetry is why the analyst hit it on a real certificate, could not reproduce it on a fresh one, and why a later retry "just worked" (the cache entry had expired by then). Also note uploads deliberately bypass static-file middleware (`Program.cs:658-671`), so the `OnPrepareResponse` cache policy at `:674-686` never applied to them — these responses fell through with no policy at all.

**Why it only bites signed-in users.** Anonymous responses happen to pick up `Cache-Control: no-cache,no-store` from the cookie-authentication handler, which masks the bug for public viewers. **Authenticated** responses — i.e. the analyst on Edit — carried no `Cache-Control` whatsoever. Confirmed empirically against the unmodified `PreviewThumbnail` control endpoint (same `PhysicalFile` pattern): authenticated 200 + `Last-Modified` + **no `Cache-Control`**.

**Fix.** Two independent layers, either of which closes it:
1. `SetUploadRevalidationHeaders()` (`CertificateController.cs:2229-2233`) emits `private, no-cache, must-revalidate` from both `ViewCertificateImage` and `ViewCertificateFile`. `no-cache` does not forbid caching — it forces revalidation before reuse, and `PhysicalFile` already sends `Last-Modified`, so an unchanged file still costs only a 304. `private` additionally keeps shared caches out, which matters because the *same URL returns different bytes per role* (see `FileAccessAllowed`) — a shared cache could otherwise serve an Analyst's copy to an anonymous caller.
2. A `?v=` cache-busting token (`Extensions/UploadCacheBusting.cs`, applied in all four views) derived from the stored upload path, so the URL itself changes whenever the file changes. This also defeats any intermediary/CDN cache that ignores request-time revalidation. The token is a truncated SHA-256 of the path rather than the filename itself — filenames are deliberately unguessable (DEF-193) and must not leak back out in a query string.

**Companion fix (same change).** `Services/FileUploadService.cs:99` and `:166` built collision filenames with `{Guid.NewGuid():N}[0..8]` — the `[0..8]` sat *outside* the interpolation hole, so the literal characters `[0..8]` were written into the filename instead of truncating the GUID. Corrected to `{Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")[0..8]}`. Cosmetic (names were still unique), but it would have produced awkward filenames on disk in the collision path.

**Scope / not touched.** No change to the save path, the 8-state workflow, the upload-path resolver, the access gate, or any API contract. `/api/v1/certificates*` untouched.

**Verification.** Build clean (0 errors; 56 pre-existing warnings unchanged). Verified authenticated on localhost:5101 as `jane.analyst@anukiconsulting.com`:
- `ViewCertificateFile/49` → **200 with `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, must-revalidate`** (pre-fix: header absent).
- Control endpoint `PreviewThumbnail` (deliberately unmodified) → 200 + `Last-Modified` + **no `Cache-Control`**, demonstrating the pre-fix condition.
- `/Certificate/Edit/26-0174` → renders `ViewCertificateImage/88?v=47c650b1`; `/Certificate/Edit/25-8760` → `ViewCertificateImage/49?v=8b537575` — token present and distinct per stored path.

**End-to-end verification — ✅ 10/10 PASS** (`Scripts/smoke-prod/def310-replace-document-verify.js`, new). Runs the complete client-reported scenario against a **real certificate with real PDFs**: creates cert `26-1733` with a generated PDF reading "DOCUMENT ALPHA", records the preview URL + a hash of the served bytes, then edits it, replaces the PDF with "DOCUMENT BRAVO", saves, and re-reads the page exactly as the analyst would.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| certificate created with PDF A | `26-1733` |
| preview rendered after create | `/Certificate/ViewCertificateImage/175?v=3313408a` |
| PDF A thumbnail served | 200, image/png, 7985b, hash `74d5ffec9b54741d` |
| revalidation `Cache-Control` present | `private, no-cache, must-revalidate` |
| preview URL changed after replace | `?v=3313408a` → `?v=c789f5a6` |
| PDF B thumbnail served | 200, 9036b, hash `0e7a3cb174603c14` |
| **rendered document changed (the reported defect)** | **hash differs — new document shown** |
| "View" control points at the refreshed URL | `openImageZoom('/Certificate/ViewCertificateImage/175?v=c789f5a6')` |
| warm-cache re-fetch returns the NEW document | matches PDF B |

The warm-cache row is the one that matters most: it primes the browser cache and then re-fetches with the *default* cache mode — the exact condition that produced the client's stale preview — and still gets the new document. **Visual ground truth:** the served thumbnail was saved to `Scripts/smoke-prod/_results/def310-current-thumbnail.png` and renders "DOCUMENT BRAVO", confirming the pixels changed, not just the bytes.

Note the "View" control uses the same thumbnail URL as the preview (there is no PDF viewer anywhere in the app — see the 2026-07-20 zoom ruling), so both surfaces the client named are covered by the one fix.

**Harness note.** Getting this to run surfaced two things worth remembering for the next Create-form automation: the `CertificationTypeId` select is `display:none` (wrapped by the `SearchableSelect` widget) so Playwright's `selectOption` refuses to drive it — set the value through the DOM and dispatch `change`; and `validateCertDateRange()` **silently** blocks the submit event if Effective and Expiration are equal, which presents as "the click did nothing" with no visible error.

**Regression test.** On a certificate whose document was uploaded well in the past: replace the PDF on Edit, save, and confirm the preview *and* the "View" control both show the new document immediately — no hard refresh, no second attempt. Repeat in a browser with a warm cache for that certificate.

### DEF-311 — Edit Certificate: pre-saved Certificate Tags can't be removed — clicking the tag's "×" does nothing, yet Save reports "updated"

**Date:** 2026-07-20 | **Status:** Fixed (`wwwroot/js/certificate-create.js`) — working tree, **pending next deploy bundle** | **Severity:** Medium — an analyst cannot remove an existing internal OR external tag on the Edit form: the pill won't clear when its "×" is clicked, and because the hidden field is never touched, Save posts the unchanged tag list but still shows the green "certificate updated" toast — so the user believes the tag was removed when it was not (silent no-op edit, data disagrees with the confirmation). No data corruption. | **QC Ref:** internal — client observation | **Reporter:** Shawn relaying client, on the Certificate Edit page: *"Editing in the Certificate Tags section (for both internal and external tags) — I selected a tag, saved, then edited to remove tag. On the edit page, the tag you're trying to remove doesn't disappear when you click the '×' on it; when you save anyway it shows the entry was updated."* (**CP NOTE: "Agreed this is issue, I encountered issue as well."**)

**Symptom.** On `/Certificate/Edit/{number}`, a tag that was saved on a prior visit renders as a pill in the Certificate Tags sidebar (External or Internal). Clicking the pill's "×" does nothing — the pill stays. Saving reports success but the tag association is unchanged. Adding-then-removing a brand-new tag *within the same session* worked; only **pre-saved** tags (and, see below, tags re-rendered after a validation error) were stuck.

**Root cause.** Two separate tag-tracking arrays that never synced. `wwwroot/js/certificate-create.js` defines a **private** `TagManager` closure holding the real `externalTags` / `internalTags` arrays; its `removeTag()` (exposed as `window.CertificateCreate.removeTag`) operates on *those* arrays. But `TagManager` itself was **not** on the exposed public API object (`window.CertificateCreate = { … }`, ~line 1366). `Views/Certificate/Edit.cshtml`'s existing-tag loader does `window.CertificateCreate.TagManager = window.CertificateCreate.TagManager || { externalTags: [], internalTags: [] }` — with `TagManager` unexposed this evaluated to a **brand-new plain object**, so the pre-saved tag IDs were pushed into that throwaway object while the real closure arrays stayed `[]`. Clicking "×" → `removeTag('35','internal')` → `internalTags.indexOf(35)` on the *real* (empty) array → `-1` → the whole removal block (splice + DOM `.remove()` + hidden-input rewrite) is skipped. Nothing happens; the hidden field keeps its server-rendered value, so Save re-posts the original list.

**Fix.** One line: expose the real closure instance on the public API — `TagManager: TagManager,` added to `window.CertificateCreate`. Now the Edit loader's `|| {…}` resolves to the *same* object `removeTag` reads, so loaded tags land in the arrays removal checks. No view, controller, service, model, API, or migration change. Build clean (0 warnings / 0 errors).

**Companion bug fixed by the same line.** `Views/Certificate/Create.cshtml`'s `restorePostedTags()` (repopulates tags after a server-side validation error re-renders the Create form) used the identical `window.CertificateCreate.TagManager || {…}` pattern and had the same defect — restored tags couldn't be removed after a failed Create POST. Exposing the real `TagManager` repairs both the Edit (pre-saved) and Create (post-validation restore) paths.

**Verification.** ✅ VERIFIED live on localhost:5101 (2026-07-20), authenticated as analyst (`jane.analyst@anukiconsulting.com`), on `/Certificate/Edit/26-0175` (a cert carrying external tag id=1 "APR" + internal tag id=35 "PL/BE"). Confirmed the loaded tags now sit in the exposed `window.CertificateCreate.TagManager` arrays (`externalTags=[1]`, `internalTags=[35]`, matching the rendered pills and hidden inputs). Firing the pill's real "×" `onclick` for **both** tags: external → pill removed, `externalTags` `[1]`→`[]`, `externalTagsHidden` `[1]`→`[]`; internal → pill removed, `internalTags` `[35]`→`[]`, `internalTagsHidden` `[35]`→`[]`. Pre-fix these clicks were confirmed no-ops (root cause above). No certificate was saved during the test — the DOM-only exercise leaves 26-0175's stored data untouched (no CR needed).

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_track_every_fix_in_defect_register]], [[feedback_def_entries_note_qc_id]], [[feedback_no_chaos_rabbit_holes]] (root-caused in code before touching the browser), [[feedback_playwright_screenshots]], [[feedback_say_client_not_names]].

### DEF-312 — Import Preview: "select all" ignored the new CR-025 filter and selected every hidden row

**Date:** 2026-07-20 | **Status:** Fixed (`wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js`, `Views/Shared/_ProductIdManager.cshtml`) — working tree, **pending next deploy bundle** | **Severity:** Medium-High — a plausible click sequence imports far more rows than the analyst intended, with no confirmation step. No data loss, but a wrong-import on a large batch is expensive to unwind. | **QC Ref:** none (client). **Found by:** Anuki internal — the **Gate 1 UI audit** of deploy bundle `GCCWebApp-deploy-20260720-1250.zip` (2026-07-20). | **Reporter:** internal (pre-deploy gate).

**Origin.** Not a pre-existing bug in isolation — **CR-025 created it.** The header select-all had always operated on the whole batch, which was harmless while every row was visible. Adding the CR-025 status/search filter meant "all" and "what I can see" diverged for the first time, turning a benign blanket toggle into a hazard. Caught by the Gate 1 audit before the bundle shipped.

**Failure scenario.** Import 1,000 ASINs, 3 of which error. Click the **Errors** tile to filter down to those 3 rows. Click the header select-all checkbox. `toggleAllImportRows` flipped `selected` on **all 997 non-error rows** — the 994 the analyst could not see included. The only cue was the Apply button's count jumping from 3 to 997; nothing else on screen changed, because the other rows were `display: none`.

**Root cause.** `toggleAllImportRows()` iterated `importPreviewData` unconditionally, with no knowledge of the filter state held in `importStatusFilter` / `importSearchTerm`. The visibility predicate lived inline inside `applyImportRowVisibility()`, so there was no shared notion of "currently shown" for the toggle to consult.

**Fix.** Extracted the predicate into `importRowMatchesFilter(row)` (plus an `isImportFiltered()` helper) as the single source of truth, and made both the row renderer and `toggleAllImportRows` consult it. With no filter active, behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged (every non-error row). With a filter active, the toggle is scoped to the filtered set. Rows hidden by the filter deliberately **retain** their existing selection — the user never saw them, so we neither select nor deselect on their behalf. Any future filter dimension goes in the one predicate and both callers inherit it.

**Companion accessibility fixes (same Gate 1 audit, same file).** The CR-025 search input had no accessible name (placeholder is not a name — WCAG 2.1 AA 4.1.2) and was 14px, which triggers iOS Safari auto-zoom on focus. Added `aria-label="Search import preview rows"`, raised the input to 16px with taller padding (touch target toward the 44px minimum), added `aria-live="polite"` to the "Showing X of Y" count so filter changes are announced, and raised the count to 14px.

**Scope / not touched.** No server, API, data, or migration change. Import *execution* is untouched — this only governs which rows are marked selected in the preview. No copy changed.

**Verification.** ✅ **9/9 PASS** — `Scripts/smoke-prod/def312-select-all-scoping.js` (new). Loads the real `product-id-manager.js` in a VM sandbox with a DOM shim and drives the actual shipped methods (not a reimplementation) against a synthetic 1,000-row batch: no-filter selects 997 (unchanged); `filter=error` selects 0; `filter=modified` selects exactly the 499 modified rows with **zero** hidden `new` rows leaked; search filter selects only the 1 match; unchecking while filtered clears visible rows while hidden rows keep their selection; clearing the filter restores full-batch behaviour. **Negative control run:** the same harness pointed at a pre-fix copy of the file (via `PIM_PATH`) **fails 5 of 9**, including `leaked=498` on the hazard assertion — proving the test genuinely detects the regression rather than passing vacuously. `node --check` clean.

**Note — reference-doc drift found during this audit.** Gate 1 cites `/0_Documentation/mockups/0_0_MasterDesignGuide.html` as the design authority, but that file **does not exist anywhere in the repo**, and `UI-STANDARDS.md` lives at `docs2/claude-ref/`, not the `docs/claude-ref/` path `.claude/CLAUDE.md` points to. Gate 1 has therefore been auditing against a partially-missing standard. Not a defect in the app — logged here so it isn't lost; needs a docs fix.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_track_every_fix_in_defect_register]], [[feedback_only_requested_changes]], [[project_predeploy_agent_checklist]].

### DEF-347 — Certificate import writes Country unvalidated: any string enters the database, and one already has

**Date:** 2026-08-13 | **Status:** **Fixed 2026-08-13 — build clean, 88/88 import tests pass (27 new), zero new failures against the pre-existing 76-failure baseline. NOT deployed; preview card not yet visually validated.** | **Severity:** **Major** — not by current impact (one junk row on the test env) but by timing: it gates the **5,556-row go-live load**, where a bad country split enters at scale and silently. | **QC Ref:** **none — no QC item exists for this.** Surfaced while investigating the client's 2026-08-12 question about certificates showing more than one country (that question is [[CR-037]], not a defect). | **Found by / Reporter:** Anuki (internal).

**The defect.** CSV import assigns `Certificate.Country` as a raw string with no validation against any list:

| Path | Code | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Parse | `Services/Import/CertificateImportService.cs:1097` | `Country = GetFieldWithMapping(csv, CertificateCountryColumns)` — takes the cell verbatim |
| Create | `:1206` | `Country = csvRow.Country` |
| Update | `:1771` | `certificate.Country = row.Country` |

Nothing anywhere compares the value to `CountryList.Countries`, the static in-code list that feeds the UI dropdown (`CertificateController.cs:346, 926`). The UI is a single `<select>` (`Views/Certificate/Create.cshtml:293`) and cannot produce an invalid value — **import is the only way in, and it is wide open.**

**Evidence it is not theoretical.** Test-env `Certificates.Country`, grouped:

```
United States 68 | Germany 31 | United Kingdom 26 | Mexico 23
Canada 22 | Indonesia 1 | El Salvador 1 | Belgium 1 | Atlantis 1
```

**`Atlantis`.** That did not come from a dropdown. 174 of 228 certificates carry a country; one of them is a country that does not exist.

**Why it matters now rather than whenever.** The go-live load runs `LOCATION`→`Location`+`Country` splits over the expired/historical set (plan §87, rule revised 2026-08-13). A split that produces `"Ontario"`, `"Alberta, Canada"` or an empty-but-not-null string is **accepted silently** — there is no error, no preview warning, and no post-load signal. The defect turns every transform bug into a *data* bug that has to be found by inspection afterwards. Fixing validation first makes the transform falsifiable ([[feedback_confirm_means_falsifiable]]).

**Proposed fix (not built).** Validate `Country` against `CountryList.Countries` during import parse; surface unknown values as a **row-level warning in the import preview** rather than a hard reject, so an analyst sees them before applying rather than after — the preview surface already exists and already renders per-row issues. Case/whitespace-insensitive match; trim before compare. Keep `Country` optional (blank stays legal — 54 test-env certs have none).

**Open checks before fixing:**
1. **Does an over-length value truncate or throw?** `Country` is `nvarchar(100)` and `Location` `nvarchar(175)`; the import path's behaviour on a longer string is **unverified** — do not assume it truncates cleanly ([[feedback_denormalized_copy_width_mismatch]]).
2. **CR-187 interaction:** `NormalizedCountry` is a persisted computed column derived from `Country`, so junk propagates into the search index too. Confirm the fix upstream of the computed column, not alongside it.
3. **Clean up `Atlantis`** on the test env — data ops, and per [[feedback_data_changes_require_cr]] the CR rule still applies to real records, though the test env is pre-launch ([[feedback_prelaunch_test_env]]).

**Deliberately NOT folded into [[CR-037]].** CR-037 (multi-select countries) may be retired for free if the client answers "display is enough". This fix must ship either way, so tying it to an optional feature would make a mandatory correction hostage to a decision that may never come.

---

### Fix — built 2026-08-13

**Tolerant resolution, not exact match** — `CountryList.TryResolve` (`Models/CountryList.cs`), following the DEF-276 `TryResolveStatus` precedent. Normalises case, surrounding and internal whitespace, punctuation and **diacritics** (`FormD` decomposition, drop `NonSpacingMark` — so `Côte d'Ivoire` and `Cote dIvoire` land on the same key), then matches against the canonical list, then an alias table (`USA`/`U.S.A.`/`America` → United States; `UK`/`Great Britain`/`England` → United Kingdom; `Czechia`, `Holland`, `Burma`, `Cape Verde`, `Swaziland`, `Macedonia`, `PRC`, `Viet Nam`, …). A migration file saying `USA` is a near-miss to be **normalised**, not junk to be flagged. The canonical lookup is **built from `Countries` at static init**, so a rename in the list can never drift out of sync with the resolver.

**Warning, not error — and this required a new channel.** `CertificateImportRow.ValidationMessages` could not be reused: any entry there flips the row to `ImportRowStatus.Error` (`:1445`) and the certificate is **dropped from the import entirely**. For the go-live load, dropping a certificate over a country typo is worse than loading it with the typo visible. Added `CertificateImportRow.Warnings` / `HasWarnings` and `CertificateImportPreviewResult.WarningRows` / `RowsWithWarnings`, surfaced as an amber **Warnings** card in `Views/CertificateImport/Preview.cshtml` (above the New Certificates card, first 50 shown with an overflow note). The row imports; the analyst sees it before Apply.

**Second defect found while fixing the first — bare uppercase headers were never mapped.** `CertificateLocationColumns` and `CertificateCountryColumns` listed `CERTIFICATE_COUNTRY`, `Country`, `country` but **not** bare `COUNTRY`, while every sibling array (e.g. `StatusColumns`) carries the uppercase form. CsvHelper header matching is **case-sensitive** here — no `PrepareHeaderForMatch` is configured (`:1070`) — so a file headed `COUNTRY` imported a **blank country, silently, with no error**. Exactly this defect's theme, and the migration's own source files use `LOCATION`/`COUNTRY` headers. Added both. *This is why the first test run failed: the test fixture's `StdHeaders` has used `COUNTRY` all along, so `StdRow`'s country value had been silently discarded in every existing test.*

**Over-length guard (closes open check 1).** An unresolved value passes through raw, and a bad §87 `Location`→`Country` split can exceed `nvarchar(100)` — SQL Server would throw on `SaveChanges` and take the **whole batch** down mid-load. Values are now clipped to 100 with the shortening stated in the warning text.

**Tests — 27 new, all passing** (`GCCWebApp.Api.Tests/Unit/Services/CertificateImportServiceTests.cs`, region *DEF-347*): alias/case/whitespace/diacritic normalisation; rejection of `Atlantis`, `Wakanda`, `Ontario`, `Alberta, Canada`; blank stays legal; **unknown country warns but the row still imports as `New` with `ErrorRows` empty** (the assertion that encodes the design decision); mixed-file test asserting only the bad rows warn; over-length truncation to exactly 100. Plus `CountryList_EveryAliasTargetExistsInTheCountryList`, a guard against the mistake this fix nearly shipped with — three aliases initially pointed at spellings **not in the list** (`Korea, South` when the list says `South Korea`; `Cote d'Ivoire` when it says `Ivory Coast`), which would have imported a country the Edit dropdown cannot re-select — the [[feedback_dropdown_filtered_subset_drops_stored_value]] failure shape. *The verification that missed it grepped the whole file and matched the alias lines themselves; the corrected check greps the `Countries` block only.*

**Regression:** `GCCWebApp.Api.Tests` **76 failed / 683 passed / 759 total** with the change vs **76 failed / 657 passed / 733 total** with it stashed — **identical failure count, zero new failures**, +26 net new passing tests.

**Data cleanup — DONE 2026-08-13.** The `Atlantis` row was **certificate 26-9721** (Id 174): company `DATA4`, product *"Test Edge Product 0081 Bob's Apostrophe"*, created by **`admin.uat`** on 2026-06-17 — UAT test data, not a business record, so no CR was required ([[feedback_prelaunch_test_env]]; [[feedback_data_changes_require_cr]] applies to real records). Its `Location` is `New York, NY`, so the country was unambiguous:

```sql
UPDATE Certificates SET Country = 'United States', UpdatedAt = SYSUTCDATETIME()
WHERE Id = 174 AND Country = 'Atlantis';   -- 1 row, in a transaction, guarded on the old value
-- rollback: UPDATE Certificates SET Country = 'Atlantis' WHERE Id = 174;
```

CR-187's persisted `NormalizedCountry` recomputed automatically (`atlantis` → `unitedstates`), confirming the computed column tracks the fix. The test certificate was **not** deleted — its product name is a deliberate apostrophe-handling edge case still worth keeping. **Full-column re-audit after the update: all 8 remaining distinct `Country` values on the test env resolve against `CountryList`.** Note the direct SQL bypassed `AuditService`, so there is no audit row for this correction — acceptable for a UAT record, not acceptable as a pattern for real data.

**Still open after this fix:**
1. **Preview card not visually validated** — asserted through the service layer, not through a browser ([[env_local_dev_server_and_chrome]]). Needs a look on localhost before deploy.
2. **`Location` has no equivalent validation** and is `nvarchar(175)`. It is free text by design so there is no list to check it against, but the same over-length risk exists on the §87 split. Not addressed here.
3. **Code fix and data fix are now out of step** — the data correction is live on the test env, the code fix is local only. Until this ships, the test env is clean but still able to accept a new bad value on the next import.

**Related:** [[CR-037]] · [[DEF-276]] (tolerant status resolution — the pattern copied) · `migration-import-transform-plan-2026-06-22.md` §87 · `docs/tracking/CR-037-multi-country-certificates.md` §8.

### DEF-346 — Product ID export writes pipe-delimited partners under a heading that tells the user to use commas

**Date:** 2026-08-10 | **Status:** **Fixed 2026-08-10 — verified against the live endpoint, not yet deployed.** | **Severity:** Minor (client-visible copy/data consistency) — but it sits directly on **QC #171**, which has been closed and reopened **three** times. | **QC Ref:** **#171** (Reporter: client, opened 2026-05-05; re-flagged 7/30 and 2026-08-07). **Found by:** Anuki — surfaced as advisory finding A1 of the Gate 1 pre-deploy audit for the 2026-08-10 bundle, then approved for fix by Shawn. | **Reporter:** Anuki (internal).

**How it surfaced.** [[DEF-342]] put the client's requested separator hint — `Partner (separate by comma)` — into the Product Identifiers CSV **template**. Gate 1 then noticed the **export** still emitted `Amazon|Novi`. So the template instructed commas while the export demonstrated pipes: the user is told one thing and shown another, in the same column, in the same feature. That is the same *"unclear when multiple"* confusion QC #171 has been reopened over three times, which is why a cosmetic-looking mismatch was worth closing now rather than discovering as a fourth reopen.

**Two export paths, and they were broken differently — this is the DEF-342 trap repeating.** DEF-342 was itself caused by fixing one of two templates behind two different buttons. The same shape applied here:

| Path | Used when | What it did | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ProductIdService.ExportToCsvAsync` (`:822`) — reached via `GET /api/productids/certificate/{id}/export` | **Saved certificates — the normal case** | Wrote `CertificateProductId.Partner` **raw**. That denormalized column is stored pipe-delimited (the UI saves `_partners.join('|')`, `product-id-manager.js:779`), so the pipes came from the *stored value*, not from a join. | New `FormatPartnerList()` normalises on the way **out** |
| `product-id-manager.js:2207` `exportInMemoryProductIds()` | Unsaved (new) certificates only | Joined with `'|'` | `join(', ')` |

Fixing only the client-side one would have left the path that actually runs for real certificates untouched.

**Normalised on output, deliberately — not in storage.** `FormatPartnerList` splits on `'|'` or `','` and rejoins with `", "`. Nothing stored changes: no migration, no rewrite of live rows, and the save/import path is untouched. Round-trip stays lossless because the import parser already accepts either delimiter (`getPartnerList()` splits `/[|,]/`, and the backend `SyncPartners` splits `'|'`/`','`).

**Quoting was already correct, which is the only reason this is safe.** Both paths emit every cell quoted — server-side via `CsvCell` (RFC 4180), client-side via literal `"` wrapping — so a comma *inside* the value cannot split the column. Had the cells been unquoted, this change would have corrupted every multi-partner row.

**What was NOT changed, on purpose:**
- **The export column heading stays `Partner`.** [[DEF-110]] requires the export header order and labels to match the on-screen table, whose column is `Partner`. The client's requested wording belongs on the **template** (where DEF-342 put it), not on the export.
- **`product-id-manager.js:779`** still saves `join('|')`. That is the API payload wire format consumed by `SyncPartners`, not a user-facing CSV. Out of scope.
- The pipe-joined query parameters in the tile-view scripts are URL filter params, not CSV. Untouched.

**Verification (localhost:5101, dev DB, 2026-08-10).** Build clean, 0 errors. Temporarily set `CertificateProductIds.Id = 14` to `Amazon|Novi` on dev, then drove the **real** endpoint through an authenticated admin session (reusing the security harness login rather than a stub):

```
HTTP 200
header: Type,Product ID,Status,Partner,ProductName,ProductSku,Description,CreatedAt,CreatedBy
partner cells: ["Amazon, Novi","Amazon","Amazon","Amazon"]
any pipe left in Partner column: false
rows whose column count breaks vs header: 0  (quoting intact)
```

The column-count assertion is the one that matters: it proves the embedded comma did not split the field. Dev row restored to `Amazon` afterwards; `0` rows with a pipe remain.

> **Coverage gap, stated rather than hidden:** no product ID in the dev database has a genuine multi-partner value, so the multi-partner case only exists under a value I created for this test. The fix is exercised, but not against natural data — worth a look on the client's environment after deploy.

**Gate consequence.** This change landed **after** Gates 1 and 2 had already passed the bundle, so `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js` and `Services/ProductIdService.cs` are now newer than the audit that cleared them. Gate 1 and the deterministic Gate 3/4/8 suite must be re-run before upload — see the deploy notes for the 2026-08-10 bundle.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_client_requested_labels_immutable]], [[feedback_scoping_check_adjacent_endpoints]], [[feedback_track_every_fix_in_defect_register]], [[feedback_def_entries_note_qc_id]].

### DEF-345 — Partner API rate limiting never applies: the limiter runs before authentication, so every partner key is throttled as anonymous (100/hr, bucketed by IP)

**Date:** 2026-08-06 | **Status:** **FIXED 2026-08-10 — verified on localhost:5101, not yet deployed.** See *Fix* at the end. | **Severity:** **Major (partner-facing).** Partners get 1/2 the documented throughput, share one bucket across organisations, and we send them a limit header that contradicts both developer guides. | **QC Ref:** none — found by Anuki while settling a contradiction between the Amazon Developer Guide (200/hr) and the new generic Partner API Integration Guide (2,000/hr). **Found by:** Anuki. | **Reporter:** Anuki (internal).

**How it surfaced.** `docs2/exports/PARTNER_API_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.html` §2 carried a TBD asking which rate limit to publish, because the two guides disagreed by 10×. Neither number turned out to be reachable.

**Root cause — middleware ordering.** `app.UseApiRateLimiting()` is registered at `Program.cs:599`. `app.UseAuthentication()` is at `Program.cs:695` and `PartnerApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware` at `Program.cs:698`. The limiter therefore executes **~10 middleware before anything populates `context.User`**. Inside `ApiRateLimitingMiddleware.GetRateLimitForClient()` the `context.User?.Identity?.IsAuthenticated` test at `:113` is always false for API traffic, making every branch beneath it unreachable — partner limit, generic API-key limit, admin limit, authenticated limit. Execution falls through to `:150` and returns `AnonymousLimit` (100). `GetClientIdentifier()` at `:96` fails the same test and buckets by `ip:{address}` instead of `api_key:{id}`.

Consequently **both documented numbers describe dead code**:

| Documented | Source in code | Reachable? |
|---|---|---|
| 200/hr (Amazon Developer Guide) | `Program.cs:403` — `options.PartnerApiKeyLimit = 200` | No — branch at `ApiRateLimitingMiddleware.cs:129` never runs |
| 2,000/hr (Partner Integration Guide) | `PartnerApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware.cs:143` — `RateLimitPerHour?.ToString() ?? "2000"` | No — claim is never read, branch at `:116` never runs |
| **100/hr, per IP** | `ApiRateLimitingMiddleware.cs:150` — `AnonymousLimit` | **Yes — this is what actually happens** |

**Verification (localhost:5101, dev DB, 2026-08-06).** Three requests to `/api/v1/certificates` from one IP:

| # | Auth | HTTP | `X-RateLimit-Limit` | `X-RateLimit-Remaining` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | none | 401 | 100 | 98 |
| B | invalid key | 401 | 100 | 97 |
| C | **valid partner key (`PartnerApiKeys.Id = 6`)** | **200** | **100** | **96** |

The counter ran **98 → 97 → 96 across all three**. The authenticated call did not get its own bucket — it kept consuming the anonymous one. That is the decisive evidence: were limits keyed by API key, call C would have started a fresh counter at 99.

**Impact.**

1. **Throughput is half what Amazon was told** and 1/20th of what the draft partner guide promised.
2. **Cross-partner interference.** Bucketing by IP means every partner behind a shared cloud NAT egress — plus all anonymous public traffic from that address — competes for one 100/hr allowance. One partner can exhaust another's quota, and neither has any way to see why.
3. **We contradict ourselves on the wire.** Every response already carries `X-RateLimit-Limit: 100` while both guides state otherwise.
4. **The per-key override has never worked.** All five rows in `PartnerApiKeys` (dev) have `RateLimitPerHour = NULL`, so even after the ordering fix every partner lands on the fallback until a value is set.

**Secondary finding — wrong doc comment.** `Models/PartnerApiKey.cs:69` documents `RateLimitPerHour` as "null = no rate limit", but null resolves to the hardcoded `"2000"` fallback, not unlimited. Moot while the ordering bug stands; misleading once it is fixed.

**Decision (Shawn, 2026-08-06): the published partner limit is 200/hour** — i.e. the value already in `Program.cs:403`. The fix therefore makes reality match the Amazon guide, and `PARTNER_API_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.html` §2 has been set to 200 accordingly.

**Fix direction (not yet applied).** Move `app.UseApiRateLimiting()` from `Program.cs:599` to below `Program.cs:698`, so the limiter sees partner claims. This is a one-line move but it simultaneously activates *every* dormant branch — admin jumps to 5,000/hr, authenticated users to 500, generic API keys to 1,000 — so it needs a regression pass over `/api` rather than a drive-by edit. Confirm afterwards that `X-RateLimit-Limit` reads 200 for a partner key and that the counter is keyed per key, not per IP (re-run the A/B/C probe above; call C must start a fresh bucket).

> **Do not publish the partner guide until this lands.** §2 states 200/hr while the server sends 100 — shipping the doc first hands a partner a number we do not honour.

---

## Fix (2026-08-10) — verified locally, **not yet deployed**

**Two changes were required, not one.** The ordering move alone would have produced 2,000/hr, not the agreed 200.

1. **Ordering.** `app.UseApiRateLimiting()` moved from `Program.cs:599` to below `PartnerApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware`, and above `UseAuthorization()` so throttling still applies to callers who authenticate but are then denied. A comment at the old site records why it must not live there.
2. **The hardcoded fallback that shadowed configuration.** `PartnerApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware.cs:143` emitted `RateLimitPerHour?.ToString() ?? "2000"` — and since every key's column is NULL, *every* key would have reported 2,000/hr the moment the claim became readable, permanently overriding `Program.cs:403`. The claim is now emitted **only when the column has an explicit value**, so NULL falls through to `RateLimitOptions.PartnerApiKeyLimit` (200). Configuration is now the single source of truth and the column is a genuine per-key override.
3. **`Models/PartnerApiKey.cs:69` comment corrected** — NULL means "platform default", never meant "unlimited".

**Verification (localhost:5101, dev DB, 2026-08-10).** Build clean, 0 errors. Same probe as the diagnosis:

| # | Auth | HTTP | `X-RateLimit-Limit` | `Remaining` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | none | 401 | 100 | 96 |
| B | invalid key | 401 | *(none — see regression below)* | — |
| C | **valid partner key** | 200 | **200** | **199** |
| C2 | valid key again | 200 | 200 | **198** |
| A2 | none | 401 | 100 | **95** |

**The assertion this defect asked for now holds:** call C starts a fresh bucket at 199 instead of continuing the anonymous counter. The buckets are provably independent — C→C2 ran the partner counter 199→198 while the anonymous counter was untouched, and A2 then resumed at 95 exactly where A stopped. Per-key bucketing at 200/hr.

### Regression introduced by this fix — invalid keys are no longer throttled by this middleware

`PartnerApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware` short-circuits with 401 and never calls `_next` for a bad key (`:68-88`). With the limiter now below it, **invalid-key requests are neither counted nor throttled by `ApiRateLimitingMiddleware`** — visible above as row B losing its headers. Previously every failed attempt consumed the caller's IP allowance, so API-key spraying was slowed; it no longer is at this layer.

**Mitigation, and where it does not reach.** `app.UseIpRateLimiting()` (`Program.cs:648`) runs before authentication and does cover unauthenticated traffic — `*/api/*` at 60/min, 1,000/hr, 5,000/day per IP in Production. But it is wrapped in `if (!app.Environment.IsDevelopment())`, so **in Development there is now no throttle on invalid-key attempts at all.** Production, Staging and Test all set `EnableEndpointRateLimiting: true` and retain the backstop.

**Not attempted deliberately.** The reflex fix — registering the limiter both before and after authentication — double-counts valid partner traffic against the anonymous IP bucket and would reinstate the 100/hr ceiling this defect just removed. A correct version needs single-increment-per-request semantics with a re-keyed bucket after identity resolves. Left for a decision rather than guessed at.

**Also worth noting for capacity planning:** the per-IP ceiling (1,000/hr) now sits above the per-partner limit (200/hr), so partners sharing a cloud NAT egress begin contending at roughly five partners deep. Not a defect; a number to remember when onboarding.

### Regression pass (2026-08-10) — clean across four layers

**1. .NET suite — no regressions, proven by differential run rather than by matching totals.** 657 passed / 76 failed / 733 with the fix. The 76 failures land in `PartnerApiScopingTests` and `MultiPartnerApiIntegrationTests` — *the exact area this fix touches* — so a matching count was not good enough. Stashed the three changed files, re-ran at HEAD, and diffed the failing test names: **76 baseline vs 76 with-fix, zero new, zero fixed, name-for-name identical.** Sample failure message is byte-identical in both runs (`Expected data.GetArrayLength() to be 2 ... but found 0`) — an empty seed fixture, the known DEF-326 signature, not an auth or 429 failure.

**2. Security P0 gate — GREEN.** `Scripts/smoke-prod/_security/run-all.js`: partner-isolation 21P, rbac-matrix 24P, idor-download 2P, cert-detail-scoping 10P = **57P / 0F / 0W / 0B**.

**3. Amazon contract diff (Gate 4) — `CONTRACT UNCHANGED`.** 7 passed / 0 failed against the frozen April baselines. This mattered more than usual here: the fix alters the partner authentication path, and [[feedback_amazon_api_immutable]] freezes the `/api/v1/certificates*` shape.

**4. New spec pinning the activated branches.** `Scripts/smoke-prod/_security/def338-rate-limit-tiers.js` — **5 PASS / 0 FAIL / 1 WARN**:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| anonymous → `AnonymousLimit` | 100 ✅ |
| partner key → `PartnerApiKeyLimit` | HTTP 200, 200 ✅ |
| **partner and anonymous are independent buckets** | partner 199→198 (limit 200) while anon 98→97 (limit 100) ✅ |
| analyst → `AuthenticatedLimit` | 500 ✅ |
| admin → `AdminLimit` | 5,000 ✅ |
| invalid key unthrottled | **WARN** — known regression, pinned deliberately |

Every one of those four tiers had never executed before this fix; the spec exists so they cannot silently drift again. The invalid-key row is recorded as **WARN rather than FAIL** because it is a known accepted state — and it is written to flip to PASS with a "update the register" message if the gap is ever closed, so it reports the change instead of quietly going green.

> **Not wired into `run-all.js`.** The spec reads the partner key from `DEF338_PARTNER_KEY`; without it the partner rows go BLOCKED, and `run-all.js` exits non-zero on any BLOCKED. Adding it as-is would turn the P0 deploy gate red on every machine that does not export the key. Run it standalone, or decide how the suite should source a partner key before adding it to `SPECS`.

**Still to do before this closes:** deploy, re-run the tier spec against the deployed server (per [[feedback_verify_deployed_asset_not_symptom]] — a local pass is not proof the deployed asset behaves), then delete the BLOCKED block from `PARTNER_API_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.html` §2. The invalid-key regression remains open and needs its own decision.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_track_every_fix_in_defect_register]], [[feedback_amazon_api_immutable]], [[feedback_confirm_means_falsifiable]], [[feedback_verify_deployed_asset_not_symptom]], [[feedback_scoping_check_adjacent_endpoints]].

### DEF-337 — Delete recoverability: cascade children are destroyed unaudited, and the system's core entity (Certificate) has no delete audit at all

**Date:** 2026-08-04 | **Status:** **FIXED 2026-08-04 — deployed 2026-08-04.** (This entry was originally logged as "not fixed"; the fix landed the same day in two passes — see *Fix* at the end.) | **Severity:** **Major (data-loss / recoverability).** | **QC Ref:** none — found by Anuki while restoring a mistaken delete during QC #242 follow-up. **Found by:** Anuki. | **Reporter:** Anuki (internal).

> **CORRECTION 2026-08-04 — this entry's original claim was WRONG and is retracted.**
> It asserted the audit snapshot "captures only 8 of 16 columns" and that `ProductTypeId` was
> unrecoverable. **Not true.** `AuditService.BuildEntitySerializerOptions` sets
> `DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull` (`Services/Audit/AuditService.cs:491`),
> so **NULL fields are omitted by design — an absent key means NULL, not "not captured."**
> The blob for products 100/101 was therefore *complete*: those products genuinely had
> `ProductTypeId`, `Sku`, `Upc`, `Asin`, `Description`, `Model` all NULL. The restore was
> **faithful, not lossy**. Scalar-field capture on delete is sound; the real gaps are below.

**How it surfaced.** Two products (`Id 100`, `101`, both `Test Carly`, company 29 `TEST`) were deleted from the admin UI on 2026-08-04 by mistake, then restored from the audit snapshot.

**What is genuinely broken.**

**1. Cascade children are destroyed with no audit record — truly unrecoverable.** `ProductIdentifiers.ProductId` and `ProductTag.ProductsId` are both `ON DELETE CASCADE`. When a product is deleted, those rows vanish at the SQL layer, and the audit writes nothing for them. Compounding it, `BuildEntitySerializerOptions` deliberately strips navigation **collections** from the blob (`AuditService.cs:521-525`), so the parent's snapshot does not carry them either. Nothing anywhere records what the child rows were. (In this incident there were none — verified — so nothing was lost. The exposure is general.)

**2. `Certificate` — the system's core entity — has no delete audit whatsoever.** `Services/CertificateService.cs` never references `_auditService`. A deleted certificate leaves no snapshot to restore from, and its `CertificateProductIds`, `CertificatePartners` and status history go with it. This is the single largest recoverability hole in the system, and it is far more serious than the product case that exposed it.

**3. Delete-audit coverage is inconsistent across entities.** Only four paths write a DELETE record: `ProductController.cs:532`, `AdminService.cs:659` (User — and that one is a *soft* delete, so it is genuinely recoverable), `CompanyService.cs:174`, and `CertificateImportService.cs:1004` (import undo). **ProductCategories, ProductTypes, CertificationTypes and Tags write no audit row on delete at all** — which is why, earlier the same day, the audit log could neither confirm nor deny whether a category had been deleted; only row counts could settle it.

**4. Products are hard-deleted despite having an `IsDeleted` column.** `Products.IsDeleted` exists and is `NOT NULL`, but the delete path physically removes the row. Same recoverable-delete gap as [[DEF-288]] (certificates), on a table already carrying the column to avoid it. Users already do this correctly (soft delete) — the pattern exists in the codebase and simply is not applied here.

**5. `UpdatedAt` is excluded from every snapshot** via `AuditSkipFields` (`AuditService.cs:414`). Minor and arguably intentional, but it means a restore cannot reproduce the original modification timestamp.

**Suggested direction.** Extend delete-audit coverage to every deletable entity; capture cascade children before the parent goes (or make the deletes soft so nothing cascades); and prefer soft delete wherever an `IsDeleted` column already exists. Decide alongside [[DEF-288]] — same decision, several tables. Full options and trade-offs: `docs/tracking/audit-restore-improvement-proposal.md`.

---

## Fix (2026-08-04, two passes)

**Pass 1 — cascade children and the certificate hole.** Added `IAuditService.LogEntityDeleteWithChildrenAsync`, which writes the parent DELETE plus one row per cascade child in a single `SaveChanges`. Wired into `CertificateService.DeleteCertificateAsync` (four FK child tables) and four `AdminService` taxonomy deletes. Also fixed the failure mode that hid the original problem: an unresolvable `ChangedBy` now refuses loudly instead of throwing inside `SaveChanges` and being swallowed.

**Pass 2 — the gaps pass 1 left, found by a follow-up review on Shawn's instruction to "ensure there is coverage if the client needs to revert a record".**

1. **Join tables were still uncaptured.** Pass 1 captured FK children (rows with a real `CertificateId` column) but not the many-to-many join tables, which are EF skip navigations with shadow join entities — no CLR type to query, nothing to serialize, and they cascade just the same. For a certificate that silently lost `CertificateTags`, `CertificatePartners` and `CertificateCertificationTypeSubcategories`. **The partner one is the consequential one: restoring a certificate without its partner links silently changes who can see it** rather than failing visibly. New `AuditJoinRowCollector` captures each association as an `AuditLinkRow` carrying the physical join table and *both column names*, read from the EF model rather than hard-coded, so the audit trail stays correct if the mapping changes and a restore script can actually be written from it. Also covers `CertificateProductIdPartners` (CR-171 Phase 2), which cascades one level deeper.
2. **Bulk certificate delete was entirely unaudited** — `PerformBulkActionAsync("delete")` did a raw `RemoveRange`. Now deletes through `DeleteCertificateAsync` per id, so bulk and single deletes audit identically by construction rather than by duplicated code. Non-existent ids remain a no-op, not a failure.
3. **The whole v1 API deleted unaudited** — `CertificatesController`, `BulkCertificatesController` and `ProductsController` never referenced `IAuditService`. Certificate deletes now delegate to the service; product deletes capture and audit in place.
4. **Nine more unaudited delete paths closed:** `AdminService` — `DeleteRoleAsync` (now captures which users held the role and what it granted), `DeleteCertificateFieldAsync` (**captures the `CustomFieldValues` it cascades — real certificate data, not configuration; this was the most damaging one**), `DeleteCSFAttributeAsync` (routed through the audited tag path), `DeletePartnerAsync`, `DeletePathwayAsync`, `DeleteProductAsync`; plus `ProductIdService.DeleteProductIdAsync`, `ProductIdService.BulkDeleteProductIdsAsync` (used `ExecuteDeleteAsync`, a set-based SQL DELETE — rows never enter the change tracker, so they had to be snapshotted *before* the call), and `PartnerApiKeyService.DeleteApiKeyAsync`.
5. **Product hard-delete now captures its cascade children** (`ProductIdentifiers` + tag links) via shared `ProductDeleteAudit`, and audits **before** `SaveChanges` instead of after — the previous ordering meant the children were already destroyed by the time the audit ran and could no longer be read. This is the exact path that deleted products 100/101.
6. **Credential fields excluded from snapshots.** `ApiKey`, `Key`, `KeyHash` added to `AuditSkipFields` alongside `PasswordHash` when API-key deletes became audited — `PartnerApiKey.ApiKey` holds the key in plaintext and an audit blob is a long-lived, widely-readable copy. Consequence is intentional: a deleted key cannot be reconstructed from the audit trail. A revoked key should never be restored anyway.
7. **`LogEntityChangeAsync` / `LogAuditEventAsync` now resolve the acting user** the same way the delete path does, instead of writing `userId = 0` straight through to an FK violation swallowed by the catch.

**Deliberately NOT audited:** `FileUploadService` line ~368 removes a `CertificateDocument` it created moments earlier when a virus scan fails. That is a compensating rollback inside a single upload, not a user-visible delete — auditing it would add noise with nothing to restore.

**API-key callers — resolved via a configured service account.** `AuditHistory.ChangedBy` is `NOT NULL` with an FK to `Users`, and an API key has no user behind it, so v1 API deletes cannot be attributed without *some* user id. Rather than make the column nullable (which would weaken every other audit row) or hard-code an id, `AuditService` falls back to a service account named in configuration as **`Audit:SystemUserEmail`**.

**Set 2026-08-04 (Shawn) to the admin account: `swest@anukiconsulting.com`** in `appsettings.json` (base config, so it applies to every environment). Verified present and `active` as `Users.Id = 1`, `Username = 'admin'`, on **both** the dev DB (`GCCDatabase_Dev`) and the deployed test/prod DB (`gccwebap_certificates`) — so one base value is correct everywhere and no per-environment override is needed. API-initiated deletes are now audited and attributed to that account; an explicit signed-in user always takes precedence, so this never masks a real actor.

> **Operational note.** This makes the audit trail depend on a config value. If that account is ever renamed, deleted or its email changed, resolution fails **closed** — a warning is logged and the delete proceeds *unaudited*. Worth including in the account-hygiene checks before production cutover. `DEF337_AuditSystemUserFallbackTests` pins all four behaviours (resolves / unset / missing account / explicit user wins).

**Verification.** `GCCWebApp.Api.Tests/Unit/Services/DEF337_DeleteAuditCoverageTests.cs` (11) + `DEF337_AuditSystemUserFallbackTests.cs` (4) — **15 tests, all passing**, asserting the *contract* (a delete must leave a restorable record) rather than the implementation, so a future entity whose delete path forgets to audit fails here. Pass 2 added five: partner/tag link capture, link rows carrying join table + column names, bulk delete auditing every certificate, custom-field values captured, role user/permission links captured. Full suite **653 passed / 76 failed / 729 total** — the 76 are the pre-existing DEF-326 fixture failures, unchanged, none in a delete or audit path.

**Still open — the client cannot act on any of this.** There is no audit history screen and no restore action; every revert remains a hand-written SQL script. Logged as **CR-034**, because it is new functionality rather than a defect.

**Related.** `Scripts/data-ops/2026-08-04-restore-products-100-101.sql` — restore committed 2026-08-04 (test env), both rows back, faithful to the snapshot.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_data_changes_require_cr]], [[reference_testenv_sql_delete_gotchas]].

### DEF-326 — Partner-isolation tests passed vacuously: absence assertions were satisfied by an empty result set

**Date:** 2026-07-31 | **Status:** Fixed (`GCCWebApp.Api.Tests/Integration/PartnerApiScopingTests.cs`) — test-only change | **Severity:** **High (assurance defect).** No product code is wrong, but the control guarding partner data isolation was reporting green while proving nothing. | **QC Ref:** none — found by Anuki during the 2026-07-31 test-suite triage. | **Reporter:** Anuki (internal).

**What was wrong.** Most isolation assertions in `PartnerApiScopingTests` take the form *"enumerate the returned certificates and prove none belong to another partner"*. Over an **empty** array that loop body never runs, so the test passes without testing anything.

The fixture stopped returning data at some point (cause still unidentified — see `docs/tracking/test-suite-triage-2026-07-31.md`). The suite split cleanly along that fault line:

- **Every test asserting data IS returned → failed.** `ReturnsTwoCertificates`, `IncludesProductIdentifiers`, `AmazonCodeFieldPopulated`, …
- **Every test asserting data is ABSENT → passed.** `DoesNotReturnNoviOrOtherCertificates`, `NeverReturnsNonePartner`, `AllReturnedCertsMatchPartner`, `ReturnsEmptyDueToScoping`, …

`AllReturnedCertsMatchPartner` is the clearest case: it iterates the returned certificates and checks each one's `partner` field. Over zero rows that is a no-op that reports success.

**Why it matters more than the red tests.** These are the tests that guarantee [[feedback_partner_data_isolation]] — that Amazon never sees Novi's certificates and vice versa, the property DEF-103 and DEF-198 were built to enforce. **They would have kept passing if partner isolation broke completely.** The suite failed closed (nothing was over-shared, so there is no evidence of a live leak) but it was providing false assurance on the most sensitive behavior in the product.

**Fix — make emptiness a failure wherever it would make an assertion meaningless.**
- Added `RequireNonEmptyData(doc, because)`: asserts the response carries a `data` array and that the array is non-empty, with a message naming the vacuity risk. Used in place of a bare `GetProperty("data")` in every absence-asserting test.
- **Positive controls** for the two tests that legitimately expect an empty result (`Amazon_SearchByNoviSku_ReturnsEmptyDueToScoping`, `Novi_SearchByAmazonAsin_ReturnsEmptyDueToScoping`). These cannot use a non-empty guard — empty *is* the expected answer — so each now first proves the endpoint returns data for the caller's **own** product ID. Only then does the empty cross-partner result distinguish "correctly scoped out" from "this endpoint returns nothing to anyone".
- **`GetCertificateFieldNames`** returned an empty list when the array was empty, which made `AllPartners_StandardResponse_HaveSameFieldSet` compare three empty lists and pass — the most misleading green in the suite, since it claims to verify every partner receives an identical response shape. Empty is now a failure.
- **Two GS1 tests** (`GtinPaddedTo14Digits`, `StatusMappedCorrectly`) looped over an empty array. Guarded; the GTIN test additionally counts the GTINs it actually examined, because its inner `if` could skip every row even with data present.

**Result — the failure count went UP, and that is the point.**

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Suite total | 709 | 709 |
| Passing | 647 | **633** |
| Failing | 62 | **76** |
| `PartnerApiScopingTests` failures | 26 | **40** |

**14 tests moved from vacuous-pass to honest-fail.** Every other test class is unchanged (verified by class-level diff), so nothing else was disturbed. The suite now tells the truth: partner isolation is currently **unverified**, rather than falsely verified.

**Deliberately left passing.** Six tests in the class still pass and should: `NoApiKey_…_ReturnsUnauthorized`, `InvalidPartnerApiKey_…_ReturnsUnauthorized`, `SearchByProductId_InvalidType_ReturnsBadRequest` (all genuinely data-independent) and `Amazon_GetCertificates_PaginationMetadataPresent`, which checks the response envelope carries pagination metadata — legitimately true of an empty page, so forcing data there would change what the test means.

**Not fixed here:** why the fixture returns nothing. That is the separate open thread in the triage document. This change does not make the suite green — it makes it honest, which is the precondition for fixing the rest.

**Other suites checked, no change needed.** `CertificateTileExternalApiControllerTests` already pairs `Should().Contain(...)` with `Should().NotContain(...)`, so it cannot pass on an empty set; `MultiPartnerApiIntegrationTests` asserts `NotBeEmpty` on content. The vacuity was specific to `PartnerApiScopingTests`.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_partner_data_isolation]], [[project_security_regression_suite]].

### DEF-323 — Product Category usage column reported 0 products while the delete refused for exactly those products

**Date:** 2026-07-31 (**evidence corrected 2026-08-03** — original figures were taken from the dev DB, not the client's environment; see the ground-truth table) | **Status:** Fixed (`Services/AdminService.cs`) — **deployed 2026-08-04**. Covers the misreported count only; the **"see what is associated"** half of QC #242 is **still open — logged as CR-032** (see Second correction). | **Severity:** Major — the screen actively misdirects the user; the one number meant to explain a blocked delete says the blocker does not exist | **QC Ref:** **#242** (Reporter: client, opened **2026-07-30**, log status *New*). Image 107. **Found by:** client. | **Reporter:** Anuki (internal).

**Client report (7/30, verbatim).** *"I cannot delete Carly Test even though I updated all certs that are using it... The table is saying there are 2 Test Type but I can't find them to remove to then be able to remove this test item."*

**First correction: "Carly Test" is a Product CATEGORY, not a Product Type.** It is `ProductCategories.Id = 9` on both dev and the test environment, and it has **zero** product types under it.

**Measured ground truth — CORRECTED 2026-08-03 to the TEST ENVIRONMENT** (`gccwebapp.com` → `gccwebap_certificates`), which is the environment the client was actually using. The original entry cited **dev DB** figures (1 product / 2 certificates); those were never the client's numbers.

| Reference | Test env (client's) | Dev DB (originally cited) |
|---|---|---|
| Child ProductTypes | **0** | 0 |
| Products attached directly (`Products.CategoryId = 9`) | **2** | 1 |
| Certificates attached (`Certificates.ProductCategoryId = 9`) | **0** | 2 |

**The two products are the entire blocker, and both are fully orphaned** — 0 certificates (`Certificates.ProductId`), 0 `ProductIdentifiers`:

| Product Id | Name | Placement |
|---|---|---|
| **389** | `Carly Test` | `CategoryId = 9`, no ProductType |
| **392** | `Test` | `CategoryId = 9`, no ProductType |

**This vindicates the client's own account.** They wrote *"even though I updated all certs that are using it"* — the certificate count on their environment is genuinely **0**. They had finished the cert reassignment; only the two products remained, and those are exactly what the Usage column was reporting as 0.

**Root cause.** `GetProductTypesAsync` seeded each category node's product set as empty on an explicit — and false — assertion in the code: `var catProductIds = new HashSet<int>(); // categories have no direct products`. `Products.CategoryId` is a real FK; a product can sit directly under a category with no ProductType in between. The category's Products figure therefore only ever counted products reached *through its child types*. With zero child types, "Carly Test" reported **Products = 0**.

Meanwhile `DeleteProductCategoryAsync` checks `category.Products` — the direct FK — and refused with *"Cannot delete: N product(s) are assigned to this category."* (**N = 2** on the client's test environment; the originally-quoted *"1 product(s)"* was the dev DB's message.)

So the two halves disagreed by construction: **the display read one set of FKs and the delete pre-check read another.** The client saw Products = 0, was told products were blocking the delete, and had no on-screen number anywhere that pointed at the two rows actually holding it.

**Second correction (2026-08-03): the "2 Test Type" is a real, separate record — the original entry wrongly dismissed it as nonexistent.** There is a Product **Type** named `Test Type`, `ProductTypes.Id = 86`, sitting under category **Chemicals and Raw Materials** (`CategoryId = 1`) — *not* under Carly Test. It holds exactly **2 products**, and that is the "2" the client was reading:

| Product Id | Name |
|---|---|
| **140** | `Best Product Ever v2` |
| **141** | `Best Product Ever v3™` |

Both are likewise orphaned (0 certificates, 0 identifiers). **This case is untouched by the fix below** — products linked via `ProductTypeId` were always counted correctly, so `Test Type` displayed an accurate 2 the whole time. The client still could not act on it, because neither product name reveals it is test data and the screen shows a count with no way to reach the rows behind it. That is the residual **"or see what is associated"** half of QC #242 — logged as **CR-032** (proposed 2026-08-04). Note CR-032 was **narrowed the same day**: the root cause is data (4 live test products), not code, and the "override" idea was an internal triage note rather than a client ask. The immediate block clears via CR-019 data cleanup with no code change.

**Same failure family as DEF-196/197**, which corrected the *certificate* rollups at every node but left this product path untouched. Third time in this subsystem that a count and a guard have been sourced from different queries — see [[feedback_scoping_check_adjacent_endpoints]].

**Fix.** Collect `Products.CategoryId` into a `productIdsByCategory` lookup and seed each category node from it, then union the child-type sets on top as before. `HashSet<int>` union, so a product reachable both directly and through a child type is still counted once. Display and delete pre-check now read the same FKs.

**Expected post-deploy result on the TEST ENV** (from the 2026-08-03 read-only re-check, not yet observed in the UI because the fix has not shipped): the "Carly Test" row should read **`productCount: 2, certificateCount: 0`** — was `0 / 0`, i.e. a category the screen described as completely empty while refusing to delete it. Those 2 products are #389 and #392 above.

**Validation (localhost:5101 against the DEV DB, 2026-07-31, authed as Admin).** `/Admin/GetProductTypes` for "Carly Test" returns `productCount: 1, certificateCount: 2` (was `0 / 2`) — dev's row shape differs from the client's, but it exercises the same corrected code path. Cross-checked **all 9 active categories** against SQL ground truth (`DISTINCT` products via direct `CategoryId` ∪ `ProductTypeId` ∪ `ProductSubcategoryId`): API vs SQL — Carly Test 1/1, Chemicals 72/72, Clothing 6/6, Construction 0/0, Consumer 24/24, Electronics 8/8, Food 10/10, Healthcare 0/0, Packaging 0/0. **Exact match on every node — no inflation**, which was the specific regression DEF-197 had to fix previously.

**Linked memory.** [[feedback_scoping_check_adjacent_endpoints]], [[feedback_column_exists_but_never_projected]].

### DEF-329 — Header search on the homepage discarded every active filter, because the "am I on a tile view?" test checked the URL instead of the page

**Date:** 2026-08-03 | **Status:** Fixed (`wwwroot/js/main.js` — `initializeSearchFunctionality`) — **deployed 2026-08-04** | **Severity:** Major — silent loss of the user's filter state on the most-used entry point | **QC Ref:** none recorded. **Found by:** unknown — see provenance note. | **Reporter:** Anuki (internal).

> ⚠️ **Provenance / how this entry was written.** This change was found **already present in the working tree** during the Gate 5 traceability audit for the next deploy bundle (2026-08-03), with **no DEF or CR covering it** — the only orphan in a 24-file changeset. It was produced by a parallel work stream, not by the session that wrote this entry. The description below is **reconstructed from the diff and its own inline comment**, and the behaviour has **not** been independently re-verified here. Logged so the change is traceable rather than shipping undocumented (per the Gate 5 "no orphan changes" rule). **Whoever made the change should confirm or correct this entry, and add its QC ref if one exists.**

**Symptom (as described by the code's own comment).** Typing in the header search bar and pressing Enter on the **public tile view served at the site root `/`** hard-navigated to `/Certificate/CertificateTileView?search=<term>`, discarding every active filter — certificate type, category, company, country, tags — and the sort along with them.

**Root cause.** `initializeSearchFunctionality` decides whether to bind its own Enter handler by asking whether the tile view is *already* handling search. That test was a **URL string check**:

```js
const isTileViewPage = window.location.pathname.toLowerCase().includes('/certificate/certificatetileview');
```

The public tile view is the **default route** (`Program.cs` — `{controller=Certificate}/{action=CertificateTileView}`), so a visitor who arrives at the homepage is on that view at pathname `/`. The string test returns `false` there, `main.js` binds its generic Enter handler on top of the page's own search handling, and that handler navigates rather than filtering in place — throwing away the filter state the tile view was holding.

**Fix.** Detect the **page**, not the URL — test for a DOM element that exists on the tile views and nowhere else:

```js
const isTileViewPage = window.location.pathname.toLowerCase().includes('/certificate/certificatetileview')
    || document.getElementById('certificatesGrid') !== null;
```

`#certificatesGrid` is present on all three tile views (public / external / internal), so the same guard now covers the root-served case. The original URL check is retained, so nothing that worked before changes.

**Why this class of bug recurs here.** Route defaults mean one view has **two** valid URLs, and any behaviour keyed on the pathname silently covers only one of them. Same shape as [[feedback_scoping_check_adjacent_endpoints]] — the obvious path gets handled, the alias does not.

**Owed before this is closed:** confirm the QC ref (if any) and re-verify on the live homepage at 5 viewports per the standing Playwright rule — neither was done in the audit session that logged it.
